# Full content review — all findings (2026-10-03)

3180 findings from 51 reviewers. 38 more were dropped as false alarms after checking (listed at the end). `?` after the type means the reviewer was not sure. Nothing in this file has been changed in the app.

- **low** `en_hard` gracias-por-todo: despedida — What a nice send-off! / Are you coming to the send-off? vs 'farewell party' in the next two lines → Use 'farewell party' / 'goodbye party' in all four. _('Send-off' is an idiom and the gloss changes between lines.)_
- **low** `tip_unclear` gracias-por-todo tip cf2878f8 — never *adiós*: **me despido** with **hasta la próxima**, because here nobody really leaves. → Nobody says *adiós*: say **chau**, **nos vemos** or **hasta la próxima**. _(Mixed Spanish/English sentence is hard to parse and skips 'chau'.)_
- **high** `experience` ya-sos-de-aca (final unit) — Final unit = 6 new words (felicitaciones, acento, lograr…), 27 drills, 13 of them about 'acento' → Make the finale a real capstone: a short farewell-party dialogue mixing slang from the whole course, first-person lines, and a closing message to the learner. _(The course ends on a thin A2 vocabulary drill; not a satisfying finish.)_
- **medium** `missing` ya-sos-de-aca — Only second-person praise: lo lograste, ya sos de acá → Add the learner's own lines: '¡Lo logré!' / 'Ya soy de acá.' / 'Me siento porteño.' / 'Che, ¿ya soy de acá?' _(The learner is the one finishing; they never get to say 'I did it'.)_
- **low** `missing` ya-sos-de-aca tip bb475835 — among friends, just **¡grande!** (tip only) → Add drills: '¡Grande, lo lograste!' / '¡Grande, Sofi!' _(Best slang item of the unit is mentioned but never practised.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` ya-sos-de-aca: acento / lograr — Tenés acento porteño. / Con ese acento, ya sos de acá. / Lograr ese acento en un año es increíble. / Lograr un buen acento lleva tiempo. / ¿Cómo hiciste para lograr ese acento? → Vary what was achieved: 'Lograste entender un chiste.' / 'Lograste discutir de fútbol.' / 'Lograste hacer un asado.' _(All three 'lograr' lines and half the unit are about the accent.)_
- **low** `not_argentine` ya-sos-de-aca 0459f07e — Mirá vos, lograste tomar mate sin azúcar. → Mirá vos, lograste tomar mate amargo. _(The local term is 'mate amargo'.)_
- **low** `en_hard` ya-sos-de-aca 0459f07e, e8c491b6, c662b63c — Would you look at that, … / Getting that accent down in a year → Look at you, … / Getting that accent in a year _(Idiomatic English; plain version reads easier.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` ya-sos-de-aca: Obelisco — Obelisco=the Obelisk (new word, used in one sentence) → Drop it as a 'new word' or add 2–3 lines ('Festejamos en el Obelisco'). _(A taught word with a single drill; celebrating at the Obelisco would fit the finale.)_
- **low** `weird?` ya-sos-de-aca 88b1480b — ¡Felicitaciones, fuiste solo al Obelisco en bondi! → ¡Felicitaciones, ya viajás en bondi sin mirar el mapa! _(Congratulating a C1 adult for one bus ride sounds childish.)_
- **low** `experience?` gracias-por-todo → ya-sos-de-aca order — Unit 25 = farewell party and leaving; unit 26 = you're a local now → Swap them or merge: become a local first, then the despedida and toast close the course. _(The story says goodbye, then keeps going; the toast is the natural last scene.)_

## Course plan: topics, order and grammar


### curriculum-grammar

- **high** `missing` whole course (best place: 2.1 la-gente) — "nuestro/nuestra" appears in 0 sentences and 0 tips in all 381 units (mi 1.17, tu 1.22, su 2.1 are taught). → Add nuestro/nuestra/nuestros/nuestras to 2.1–2.2 (tip + ~10 sentences: "nuestra casa", "nuestros viejos") and recycle it later. _(A basic possessive is completely absent from an A1–C1 course.)_
- **high** `missing` whole course (best place: 3.11 este-buzo or 4.19 las-tareas) — mío/tuyo/suyo never taught. Only "lo tuyo / lo mío" as an idiom at 14.12 (C1.3). "¿De quién es?" is answered only with "es de Juan". → Add a unit pair at A2: "¿Es tuyo? — Sí, es mío / es de él", "un amigo mío", "el mío, la tuya". _(Learners cannot say "it's mine" or "a friend of mine" until C1, and then only as an idiom.)_
- **high** `missing` whole course (best place: section 3 or 5) — No tip anywhere contrasts por and para. "para" is a word at 2.15, "por" a word at 3.4; "para que" only at 9.3. → Add one unit pair (A2) with a table: para = goal, person, deadline, destination; por = cause, through, per, time of day, exchange (gracias por, por la mañana, por acá, por eso). _(Por/para is a core difficulty for English readers and is never explained.)_
- **high** `missing` section 4 (4.3 comi-y-sali / 4.4 naci-en) — No tip maps English "I have eaten / have you seen…?" to the Argentine preterite; present perfect appears 0 times and is never mentioned. → Add a tip in 4.3 or 4.7: "English 'I've already eaten' = **ya comí**; 'have you ever been?' = **¿fuiste alguna vez?** You will hear *he comido* from Spaniards and in the news; porteños don't use it." Add ya/todavía no/alguna vez/nunca sentences. _(The Argentine preterite preference is the key regional tense rule and the course never states it.)_
- **high** `missing` 3.8 dale-veni … 6.11 te-lo-devuelvo — Vos command + two pronouns (dámelo, pasámela, decímelo, mandáselo) appears in 0 sentences in the whole course. → Add to 6.11/6.12: tip "dame + lo = **dámelo**, decí + me + lo = **decímelo**, mandá + le + lo = **mandáselo**" with ~12 sentences. _(Extremely frequent everyday forms; double pronouns are taught only before conjugated verbs.)_
- **high** `missing` section 3–4 (after 3.8 dale-veni) — Ustedes commands (pasen, esperen, vengan, miren) first appear at 10.9 (B2.1); 0 uses before. → Move a short version of 10.9 to A2 (section 4 or 6): "pasen, esperen, vengan, siéntense, miren"; keep 10.9–10.10 as the hosting scenario. _(Talking to two people is an A2 need; six sections pass with no plural command.)_
- **high** `level` 14.9 un-ratito — Diminutive -ito is taught at C1.3; "ratito, poquito, cafecito, chiquito, cerquita" do not appear in any earlier unit. → Move 14.9–14.10 to A2 (section 4–6) and use un poquito / un ratito / chiquito freely from then on. _(Porteños use -ito in every second sentence; it is A2 material, not C1.)_
- **high** `level` 12.17 acabo-de — acabar de + soler first taught at C1.1; volver a and dejar de are re-taught there after 10.5–10.6. → Move soler to B1 (section 8) with habits; cut acabar de to a recognition note inside 4.3 ("recién llegué = acabo de llegar"); drop the repeat of volver a / dejar de. _(A2–B1 periphrases labelled C1; and porteños say recién, which the course itself teaches at 4.3.)_
- **high** `experience` 4.17 te-llamo — One unit (141 sentences, 1 tip) introduces direct objects lo/la/los/las, indirect le/les, me/te, and pronouns on commands; it also uses "¿Se lo mandás vos?", "Ya se lo mando" (taught 6.11). → Split: 4.17 = lo/la/los/las (things and people); 4.18 = le/les + doubling; move command clitics to their own unit; remove the 'se lo' sentences until 6.11. _(Too many new points at once at A2.1, and it uses double pronouns two sections early.)_
- **high** `level` section 13 [C1.2] — 24 of 26 units carry topic tags only (ciudad.paro, votar, robar, edificio.consorcio, futbol.hinchada, comida.parrilla). Sentences: "¿Votaste hoy?", "Se rompió el calefón.", "¿Hay piquete hoy?" → Relabel as B1–B2 topic units, or add real C1 grammar and longer sentences (relatives with prepositions, perfect subjunctive, future in headlines, nominalisation, connectors like dado que / si bien). _(Only passive with ser and lo + adjective are grammar here; sentence difficulty is A2–B1, not C1.)_
- **high** `level` section 15 [C1.4] — All 26 units have topic tags only (laburo.proyecto, viaje.argentina, cultura.mate, humor, vida.eventos). Sentences: "Nos casamos en julio, en Mendoza.", "¿Cuánto es el presupuesto?" → Call sections 13 and 15 what they are (advanced vocabulary and culture) or add C1 structures; do not sell them as C1 grammar. _(The final C1 section teaches no grammar at all and its sentences use A2 structures.)_
- **high** `level` section 12 [C1.1] — Grammar taught: reported requests (B2, repeat of 10.1), si = whether (B1, repeat of 8.21), polite requests, acabar de / soler / volver a / dejar de (A2–B1), estar podrido. → Relabel section 12 as B2.3, or replace the repeated points with real C1 grammar. Only clitico.la-idiomatico (12.13–12.14) is advanced. _(The C1.1 label is not honest: almost every grammar point is B1–B2 or already taught.)_
- **medium** `missing` section 2–4 (best place: 2.8 como-estas / 3.10 ropa-y-colores) — Ser vs estar is only contrasted as identity vs location (2.3, 2.7). No tip on ser/estar + adjective, though both are used ("está aburrido", "es re cómodo", "está listo", "La fiesta es en mi casa"). → Add a tip + sentences: es aburrido / está aburrido, es rico / está rico, es lindo / estás linda, ser listo / estar listo, and "la fiesta es en casa" (events take ser). _(The hardest part of ser/estar (adjectives, events) is left to guesswork.)_
- **medium** `missing` 4.3 comi-y-sali — conocer is introduced only as vocabulary (conozco, conocés); saber is used from 1.9. No tip contrasts saber and conocer anywhere (7.19 covers only saber). → Add a tip in 4.3 or 7.19: "**saber** = know a fact or how to; **conocer** = know a person or place; **conocí a Sofi** = I met Sofi". _(A classic contrast for English readers is never explained.)_
- **medium** `missing` section 4 (4.1 ayer-labure) — "hace + time" = ago has no tip anywhere and only ~6 sentences in the course ("Pedimos hace una hora", "Me mudé hace poco"). "Hace … que" only at 10.5 (B2.1). → Teach "hace dos años / hace un rato / hace poco" with the preterite in 4.1–4.4 (tag tiempo.hace), plus "¿hace cuánto?". _("Ago" is essential for talking about the past at A2.)_
- **medium** `missing` whole course — The personal "a" ("Conocí a Sofi", "¿A Juan? Lo vi", "Busco a alguien") is used from 4.3 on but no tip explains it. → Add a tip in 4.3 or 4.17: "A person as object takes **a**: *vi a Juan*, *llamé a mi vieja* — but *vi la película*." _(English readers leave it out; the rule is short and never given.)_
- **medium** `missing` 4.9 el-finde / 4.17 te-llamo — Doubling of le ("Le dije a Juan que no", "Le di la llave a Sofi") is used from 4.9 but never explained. → Add a tip in 4.17: "Even when you name the person, the **le** stays: *le dije a Juan*, *les mandé las fotos a mis viejos*." _(Mandatory in Rioplatense speech and contrary to English logic.)_
- **medium** `missing` 3.5 queres-podes-vas — Real conditions with si + present ("Si Juan sale temprano, vamos al cine") appear from 3.5 in 100+ units but are never a taught point; only si-hipotetico is tagged (8.3). → Add a tip + sentences at A2 (e.g. 6.3 or 5.19): "**Si** llueve, no voy. **Si** podés, avisame." — present after si, never future or subjunctive. _(The basic if-clause has no explanation, so the 8.3 contrast has nothing to stand on.)_
- **medium** `missing` whole course — demasiado and bastante: 0 sentences. No tip contrasting muy / mucho beyond weather (3.20). → Add to 3.10–3.11 or 4.11: "muy caro, mucho frío, demasiado caro, bastante bien, muchas ganas" with a tip (muy + adjective, mucho + noun/verb). _(Basic quantifiers missing; muy/mucho is a typical learner error.)_
- **medium** `missing` whole course (best place: section 10) — "sino" / "no … sino" / "no solo … sino también": 0 sentences in the course. → Add to 10.19 por-un-lado: "No es caro, sino carísimo", "No fui yo, sino Juan", plus the porteño alternative "no es X, es Y". _(A B1–B2 connector needed for arguing; course has a whole section called Making your case.)_
- **medium** `missing` section 10 (10.13 el-que-quieras) — Relative clauses with a preposition never appear: "la chica con la que salgo", "el bar al que vamos", "la razón por la que…", "con quien", "lo cual" = 0 sentences. → Add a unit pair in section 12 or 14: "el amigo con el que vivo", "el barrio en el que crecí", "la persona a la que le escribí". _(Real B2–C1 grammar that a C1 course should have; currently only el que / donde.)_
- **medium** `missing` 10.17 si-hubiera-sabido — Past si-clause is taught only as "Si hubiera sabido, te hubiera avisado". "habría + participle" occurs once in the course (14.4) and is never presented. → Add one tip line + 6 sentences: "You'll also hear and read **te habría avisado** — same meaning." _(Learners will meet habría avisado in writing and news and not recognise it.)_
- **medium** `missing` section 7 / 10 — Perfect subjunctive ("Espero que hayas llegado bien", "No creo que haya venido", "Qué bueno que hayas podido") = 0 sentences. haya appears only as 'there is'. → Add a unit pair in section 10 or 11: haya/hayas/hayan + participle after espero que, no creo que, qué bueno que, cuando hayas terminado. _(Needed to react to or doubt past events; standard B2 content.)_
- **medium** `missing` 6.19 donde-estara — The simple future is taught only as guessing; as a real future ("mañana lloverá", "el subte no funcionará") it appears 0 times, even in the news units of section 13. → Add a recognition tip + a few news-style sentences in 13.3–13.4 or 13.9: "In headlines the same form is a real future: *El paro durará 24 horas*." _(Section 13 promises reading the news, where the future tense is constant.)_
- **medium** `missing` 3.8 dale-veni — Irregular/short vos commands are never listed together: hacé, poné, tené, decí, salí, sé; and that "go" is andá (ir has no vos command). hacé/tené/decí are never taught as words. → Add a tip in 3.9 or 4.17: "ir → **andá**; hacer → **hacé**; poner → **poné**; tener → **tené**; decir → **decí**; salir → **salí**; ser → **sé**". _(Learners coming from tú-Spanish expect ve/haz/pon; the vos set must be shown explicitly.)_
- **medium** `tip_unclear` 3.8 dale-veni — Tip table: "| andar | **andá** |" while every sentence uses it as 'go' ("Andá al médico", "Andá vos"). → Add: "**Andá** is the command for *go*. *Ir* has no vos command of its own, so porteños borrow *andar*." _(The learner knows 'go' as ir (taught 3.5) and cannot connect andá to it.)_
- **medium** `missing` 3.22 el-cumple / 4.17 te-llamo — Pronoun position with two verbs is never explained ("te voy a esperar" vs "voy a esperarte", "lo estoy haciendo", "tendrías que llamarlo"). Used from 3.8. → Add a tip in 4.18: "With two verbs it goes before the first or on the end of the second: **te voy a llamar** = **voy a llamarte**." _(4.17–4.18 say 'before the verb, only a command takes it on the end', which is incomplete.)_
- **medium** `tip_wrong` 4.18 te-llame — "Before the verb, past or present. Only a command takes it on the end: **mostrame**, **buscame**." (also 4.24: "Before the verb, always — only a command…") → "Before the verb, past or present. A command takes it on the end (**mostrame**), and so can an infinitive: *voy a llamarte*." _('Only a command' is false: infinitives and gerunds take it too (quiero verte, tendrías que llamarlo).)_
- **medium** `not_argentine?` 12.17 acabo-de — 48 drill sentences with "acabo de / acaba de" ("Acaba de salir", "Acabo de llegar"). → Keep 5–6 for recognition and say in the tip: "Porteños usually say **recién**: *recién llegué*, *recién salió*." _(Drilling a form porteños rarely use, at C1, contradicts the course's own recién tip.)_
- **medium** `level` 11.19 voy-entendiendo — estar por + infinitive first taught at B2.2 ("Estoy por salir"), though 5.6 already uses "Estaba por entrar a la ducha". → Teach estar por in section 5–6 (next to ir a + inf); keep ir/andar + gerund at B2. _('About to' is A2–B1 and is used in 5.6 before being taught.)_
- **medium** `level` 11.21 me-cae-bien — caer bien/mal and llevarse bien are taught at B2.2. → Move to section 6 (next to 6.17 relaciones) or section 8 (8.17 personalidad). _(Gustar-type verb for liking people is A2–B1; without it learners say "me gusta Juan" wrongly for five sections.)_
- **medium** `level` 11.5 deberias — deberías / debería / estaría bueno is a B2.2 unit pair; 8.1 already taught the conditional and "tendrías que". → Fold deberías into 8.1–8.2 (B1.2) and replace 11.5–11.6 with new B2 grammar (e.g. perfect subjunctive). _('You should' is B1; here it comes three sections after the tense it uses.)_
- **medium** `level` 8.5 me-gustaria — "Me gustaría" is first taught at B1.2; "quisiera" only at 12.5 (C1.1). → Introduce "me gustaría + infinitive" as a fixed phrase in section 5 (5.19 plans) or 6.1 next to podrías. _(A2 survival phrase arrives late; podrías is already taught as a chunk at 6.1.)_
- **medium** `level` 6.19 donde-estara — Future of conjecture (¿Dónde estará?, with irregulars hará, vendrá, querrá) taught at A2.3. → Move to B1.3 or B2.1; at A2.3 keep only "capaz / seguro que / a lo mejor + present". _(A B1–B2 nuance taught before the present subjunctive, with irregular future stems and no base future.)_
- **medium** `level` 14.11 lo-que-pasa-es-que — "Lo que pasa es que…", "lo de…" taught at C1.3; "lo + adjective" at 13.25 (C1.2); "lo que" at 9.25. → Group all lo uses in section 9–10 (B1.3/B2.1) right after 9.25. _(These are B1 structures spread across three levels; none is C1.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` 12.3 me-pregunto-si — C1.1 tip "Si = whether: Me preguntó **si** venía" repeats 8.21 (B1.2): "Me preguntó **si venía**". → Drop the re-teach; keep only "fijate si / a ver si / no sé si" as new content, or move the pair to section 9 as review. _(Same point, same example sentence, relabelled C1.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` 12.1 me-pidio-que — C1.1 "Me pidió que le trajera algo" repeats 10.1 (B2.1), whose tip already has "Me pidió que lo llamara", "me dijo que esperara". → Merge into 10.1–10.2 and use 12.1–12.2 for something new (e.g. reported speech with pluperfect: "me dijo que ya había ido"). _(Identical grammar taught twice, two sections apart, with a higher label.)_
- **medium** `experience` 2.1 la-gente — One 41-sentence unit introduces plural subject pronouns, ser plural, tener plural and su/sus; 2.2 adds descriptive adjectives (167 sentences). → Split 2.1 into two units (nosotros/ustedes/ellos + somos/son; then tenemos/tienen + su) and balance sentence counts with 2.2. _(Four new grammar points in the first unit of A1.2 is a steep jump from section 1.)_
- **medium** `experience` 3.5 queres-podes-vas — One unit (144 sentences, 1 tip) teaches querer, poder, ir (all persons), ir a + place, salir, stem changes and verb + infinitive. → Split into (a) ir + a/al + place, (b) querer/poder + infinitive with the e→ie, o→ue rule. _(Three irregular verbs plus two structures under a single tip.)_
- **medium** `tip_unclear` 7.17 que-bueno — Unit headline "¡Qué bueno que viniste!" (indicative), but the tip says "A reaction to something + **que** → the subjunctive". → Add to the tip: "For something already done, porteños usually keep the plain past: *qué bueno que viniste*. For now or later, the subjunctive: *qué bueno que estés acá*." _(The unit's own title contradicts its rule and the learner gets no explanation.)_
- **medium** `experience` 7.1 quiero-que-vengas — Present subjunctive: 8 new triggers in section 7, but core units are short (7.3: 40 sentences, 7.4: 38, 7.11: 38, 7.14: 36) while vocab units run 130–170 (2.2, 3.10, 4.1). → Rebalance: at least 70–80 sentences for each new subjunctive/imperative unit; trim large A1 vocabulary units. _(Sentence volume goes to easy vocabulary, not to the hardest grammar.)_
- **medium** `level` section 14 [C1.3] — Grammar taught: no es que + subj (B2), mixed conditional (C1), tendría que haber (B2), -ito (A2), lo que pasa es que (B1), hacer + infinitive (B2), cuanto más (B2). → Move -ito and lo que pasa to A2/B1; label the rest B2.2–C1; add missing advanced points (por más que + past, aunque + imperfect subj, de + infinitive, sea como sea). _(One real C1 point out of seven; the course's true grammar ceiling is about B2.)_
- **medium** `experience` index (all sections) — Same point under different tag names: ir-a.infinitivo (3.22) vs ir-a-infinitivo (5.19); subjuntivo.pluscuamperfecto (10.17) vs pluscuamperfecto.subjuntivo (14.3); subjuntivo.imperfecto (8.3, 12.1) vs subjuntivo.imperfecto.querer-que (10.1); discurso-referido / .condicional / .pedido / .pregunta. → Use one naming scheme: area.form.detail (e.g. subjuntivo.imperfecto.si, subjuntivo.imperfecto.querer-que) and one tag per point. _(Any review or recycling logic keyed on tags will treat one point as several.)_
- **medium** `experience` index (sections 8–15) — Many 'grammar' tags are topics: ciudad.transito, banco, deportes, miedo, tecnologia, tramites, plata.inflacion, humor, cultura.mate, laburo.proyecto. Review tags are off-level: repaso.b1 in 8.25 and 9.26; repaso.b2 in 10.25 (B2.1 just started); repaso.c1 in 12.25. → Separate topic tags from grammar tags; give every unit at least one real grammar tag (even a recycled one); fix repaso.* labels to the level just finished. _(From section 8 on, about half the units have no grammar target, so grammar practice is unplanned.)_
- **low** `level` 3.1 la-hora — "Estoy enfermo hace dos días." / "Hace tres días que no tomo mate." (A1.3) → Remove from 3.1, or move after the point where hace + time is taught. _(Uses the B2.1 structure hace…que seven sections before it is taught.)_
- **low** `missing?` 6.19 donde-estara / section 11 — Guessing about the past is not covered: "Habrá salido", "Serían las diez", "¿Quién habrá sido?" = 0 sentences. → Add a B2 unit pair extending 6.19: habrá + participle and conditional of guessing ("tendría unos veinte años"). _(Natural follow-up to the conjecture future; would give section 11 or 13 real grammar content.)_
- **low** `missing` whole course — Adverbs in -mente are used in ~50 sentences (igualmente, lamentablemente…) with no tip on how they are formed. → Add one tip (section 6 or 8): "-mente = -ly, on the feminine form: rápida → rápidamente; porteños often just say *rápido*." _(Small, cheap rule that is never stated.)_
- **low** `missing?` 7.19 no-se — Preterite of saber (supe = found out) and stem-change 3rd persons beyond pidió (durmió, sintió, siguió, murió) are not presented as a set. → Add a tip in 5.9 or 6.21: "pedir → pidió, pidieron; dormir → durmió; sentir → sintió; seguir → siguió" and "supe = I found out". _(e→i / o→u in él/ellos preterite is a systematic rule shown only for pedir.)_
- **low** `missing` section 8–9 — "iba a + infinitive" for a plan that did not happen ("Iba a llamarte, pero…") is never a taught point; it shows up only in a note in 11.9. → Add a tip + sentences in 5.19–5.20 or 8.21: "**Iba a** ir, pero llovió" — was going to. _(Very frequent in excuses and stories; follows directly from ir a + imperfect.)_
- **low** `repetitive` 11.3 me-da-bronca — Emotion + que + subjunctive (me da bronca que, me pone nervioso que) repeats 7.17–7.18 (me molesta que, me preocupa que). → Keep the new vocabulary (me da + noun) but tag and present it as review; do not present the subjunctive as new. _(Same trigger class re-taught as if new at B2.2.)_
- **low** `repetitive` 11.13 se-alquila — "Se + él form" taught at 9.21–9.22 (se cena tarde) and again at 11.13–11.14 (se vende) with no link between the tips. → In 11.13 add: "Same *se* as *acá se cena tarde* (9.21); new: it goes plural with plural things — se venden bicis". _(Learner meets the same structure twice as two unrelated rules.)_
- **low** `repetitive` 5.19 la-semana-que-viene — ir a + infinitive and "la semana que viene" are taught at 3.22–3.23 and again at 5.19 with the same tip content. → Make 5.19 clearly about what is new (pienso + inf, tengo ganas de, present for fixed plans) and tag ir a as repaso. _(Second unit re-explains a point already taught and reviewed.)_
- **low** `tip_unclear` 6.19 donde-estara — "**Capaz**, **quizás** and **seguro que** guess with the plain present"; practice unit 6.23 is titled "Capaz que está enfermo". → Add later (7.10 puede-ser-que): "After *capaz que*, *quizás*, *tal vez* you'll also hear the subjunctive: *capaz que venga*. Both are fine." _(Learners will hear capaz que + subjunctive daily and the course never mentions it.)_
- **low** `level?` 8.3 si-tuviera — Imperfect subjunctive introduced at B1.2 immediately after the whole present subjunctive (section 7) and the conditional (8.1–8.2). → Keep, but move 8.3–8.4 to the end of section 8 and add ellos/ustedes forms; or swap with a lighter block. _(Three new verb systems in about 30 units is the steepest stretch of the course.)_
- **low** `level` 7.11 no-te-preocupes — Negative vos commands taught at 7.11, but 7.4 and 7.8 already use "No vengas a laburar hasta que te mejores", "No le pongas azúcar al mate". → Move those sentences after 7.11, or move 7.11–7.12 before 7.3. _(Negative commands appear before the unit that explains them.)_
- **low** `repetitive` 14.3 si-hubiera-ahorrado — Tags "condicional.mixto, pluscuamperfecto.subjuntivo" re-present "si hubiera + participle" from 10.17 ("subjuntivo.pluscuamperfecto"). → Present 14.3 as: you know si hubiera… (10.17); new = the result is now (tendría, estaría). Use one tag name. _(Same form under two different tag names; the tip does not link back.)_
- **low** `experience` index (unit pairs) — Both units of each pair carry the same grammar tags, and the second often adds the missing persons (e.g. 4.3 → 4.4 adds ellos; 7.1 → 7.10 adds ellos; 9.5 lacks nosotros). → State the split in tags (…singular / …plural) everywhere as done in 4.1–4.2, and check each tense has a full-person table by the end of its pair. _(Person coverage is uneven: some tenses get ellos/nosotros a few units late or only in a practice tip.)_
- **low** `experience` section 5 (5.9–5.16) and section 6 (6.5–6.18) — Long runs with no new grammar: 5.9–5.16 (restaurant, meeting up, holidays) and 6.5–6.10, 6.13–6.18 (shopping, tech, work, relationships). → Use these slots for the missing A2 points: por/para, mío/tuyo, hace = ago, ustedes commands, -ito, estar por, me gustaría, dámelo. _(A2 has room: the gaps listed above fit without making the course longer.)_
- **low** `experience` sections 1–3 — Sections 1–3 have 3 practice units each (one per block); sections 4–15 have 6 (two per block). No section-end checkpoint anywhere; units x.25–x.26 teach new content. → Add one mixed checkpoint at the end of each section (all tenses of the level), and a second practice unit per block in sections 1–3. _(Beginners get half the consolidation of advanced learners, and no level-end check exists.)_
- **low** `repetitive` 5.7 practica-de-chico … 5.26 te-acordas — imperfecto-vs-preterito / repaso.imperfecto-preterito is the target of 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.16, 5.23, 5.24, 5.25, 5.26 — nine units; tips 5.5, 5.6, 5.8 repeat the same "Estaba en la ducha cuando sonó el timbre" table. → Keep the volume but vary the angle: add contrasts not yet shown (conocí/conocía, supe/sabía, quise/quería, tuve que/tenía que). _(Lots of practice of one contrast with the same example, while meaning-change pairs are never taught.)_

### curriculum-topics

- **high** `missing` course-wide (emergencies) — No unit or words for emergencies: ayuda as a shout, ambulancia, emergencia, 'llamá a la policía', 'me perdí / estoy perdido', 'necesito un médico'. Theft only at 13.11 [C1.2]. → Add an A1.3/A2.1 unit 'Get help': ¡Ayuda!, llamá a una ambulancia / a la policía, es una emergencia, me perdí, me robaron, necesito ayuda, ¿hay un hospital cerca? _(Survival language; a traveller needs it in week one, not at C1 or never.)_
- **high** `missing` course-wide (public transport ride) — colectivo/subte/parada at 2.5, SUBE only inside the phone unit 6.9, boleto at 11.18. No unit on actually riding: '¿Este va a…?', '¿dónde me bajo?', cargar la SUBE, combinación, '¿me avisás?' → Add an A1.3 unit 'Take the bondi and the subte': cargar la SUBE, saldo, ¿este va a Palermo?, me bajo en la próxima, combinación, línea, boleto, ¿cuántas paradas faltan? _(Daily need in Buenos Aires; driving gets two units (8.9-8.10) and public transport none.)_
- **high** `missing` course-wide (accommodation) — Only 'hotel' (4.21). No habitación, reserva, hostel, check-in/check-out, 'tengo una reserva', llave/tarjeta, desayuno incluido, Airbnb/alquiler temporario. → Add an A1.3/A2.1 unit 'Check in': tengo una reserva a nombre de…, habitación, hostel, ¿a qué hora es el check-out?, ¿el desayuno está incluido?, alquiler temporario. _(First real conversation of any traveller; missing completely.)_
- **high** `missing` course-wide (phone, WhatsApp, numbers) — No WhatsApp, teléfono, '¿me pasás tu número?', chip/línea, 'te mando un mensaje', Instagram, '¿tenés Instagram?', seguir. Only audio (4.17), mensaje (2.19), grupo (5.12). → Add an A1.3/A2.1 unit 'Swap numbers': ¿me pasás tu número?, te escribo por WhatsApp, agendame, mandame un mensaje, ¿tenés Instagram?, te sigo; plus chip, línea, datos for the SIM shop. _(Argentina runs on WhatsApp; swapping contacts is how every friendship and errand starts.)_
- **high** `missing` course-wide (puteadas) — A 'talk like a local' course up to C1.4 has no swear words: pelotudo, la puta madre, mierda, carajo, forro, romper las bolas/pelotas, hinchar, la concha…, qué cagada, me cagué de risa. → Add a B1/B2 unit 'Understand the swearing' (recognise + mild use): boludo vs pelotudo, qué cagada, no rompas, la puta madre, hinchapelotas, with clear register warnings. _(Porteños swear constantly; a learner who cannot read it misses tone and intent.)_
- **high** `missing` course-wide (classroom survival phrases) — '¿Cómo se dice…?' never appears. '¿Qué significa?', 'repetime' and 'explicame' wait until 7.19-7.20 [B1.1]. → Add '¿Cómo se dice…?', '¿Qué significa…?', '¿Me repetís?', 'no entendí', 'más despacio' to 1.9 encantado. _(These phrases let a beginner keep a conversation alive; they belong in the first week.)_
- **high** `level` 3.12 cuanto-sale — '¿Cuánto sale?', pagar, plata, efectivo, tarjeta first at 3.12 (about unit 58). Numbers above 20 at 3.1. The learner orders coffee at 1.1 but cannot ask or understand a price for ~57 units. → Move a slim 'How much is it?' unit (cuánto sale, numbers to 100 and thousands, efectivo/tarjeta) into Section 1, right after 1.23 en-el-kiosco. _(Asking and understanding prices is the top survival skill for a visitor.)_
- **high** `level` 12.5 usted / 12.6 como-no-dona-rosa — 'disculpá', 'disculpame' first at 12.5 [C1.1]; 'con permiso' at 12.6 [C1.1]; 'buen provecho' at 10.10 [B2.1]. → Teach 'disculpá', 'permiso' (to get past) and 'buen provecho' in A1 (1.6 sos-turista or 2.15 me-traes-un-cafe). _(You say 'permiso' on every bus and 'disculpá' to every stranger from day one.)_
- **high** `level` 13.11 me-robaron — 'Me robaron el celu', chorro, denuncia, comisaría, 'bloquear' the card first at 13.11-13.12 [C1.2]. Grammar is plain preterite. → Move to A2.3/B1.1 (near 6.9 el-celu); keep motochorro, cuento del tío, trucho for later. _(Phone theft is the most likely emergency for a newcomer; C1 is years too late.)_
- **high** `level` 13.13 el-consorcio — expensas, plomero, calefón, canilla, inodoro, 'se tapó', 'gotea' first at 13.13-13.14 [C1.2]. → Move to A2.3/B1 next to 9.11-9.12 (no-anda / el-tecnico), which already teach 'no anda' and 'arreglar'. _(Anyone renting needs 'no hay agua caliente' in the first month.)_
- **high** `level` 13.21 la-parrilla — parrilla, vacío, jugoso, a punto, bien cocido, chimichurri, bife de chorizo, cubierto first at 13.21-13.22 [C1.2]. Summary '¿Me pasás un choripán?' is A2. → Move to A2.2 after 5.9-5.10 (restaurant, pizzería). _(Every tourist eats at a parrilla in week one; nothing here is C1 language.)_
- **high** `level` 15.11 quien-ceba — yerba, termo, bombilla, cebar, 'te convido un mate', merienda first at 15.11-15.12 [C1.4], though 'mate' is taught in unit 1.1. → Move the mate round to A2/B1 (e.g. after 3.17 or in Section 5 traditions). _(The most common social ritual is held back to the last 15 units of the course.)_
- **high** `level` 15.9 recorrer-el-pais — Patagonia, Iguazú, cataratas, glaciar, lago, nieve, Salta, Ushuaia, mochilero, acampar first at 15.9-15.10 [C1.4]. → Move to A2.1 beside 4.21-4.22 (de-viaje / las-vacaciones). _(Travellers plan these trips at A2; simple past-tense travel talk is not C1.)_
- **high** `level` 15.19 se-caso — 'se casó', casamiento, embarazada, 'se murió', nene, nena, 'se jubiló', 'se recibió', velorio first at 15.19-15.20 [C1.4]. → Move to A2.3/B1.1 (family news); keep 'te acompaño en el sentimiento', padrino, por civil for later. _('Died', 'got married', 'pregnant', 'kid' are basic words taught at the very end.)_
- **high** `repetitive` sections 4-15 practice units — 81 of 381 units are practice. From Section 4 on each section has 6, always in back-to-back pairs with the same grammar tags (e.g. 10.23+10.24: 118+116 sentences). Practice is 44% of all sentences in Section 14. → One practice unit per block (3 per section) of ~60 sentences, or make the second of each pair optional. _(Two 100+ sentence drills in a row, six times per section, will feel like a wall.)_
- **high** `experience` course-wide (unit size) — Unit length swings wildly: 1.5 has 8 sentences, 1.10 has 11, 14.1 has 22; 3.10 has 169, 2.2 has 167, 4.1 has 160, 2.10 has 157. → Target 40-80 sentences per unit: split 3.10, 2.2, 4.1, 2.10, 3.5; merge 1.5 into 1.6 and 1.10 into 1.11. _(A 'unit' can take 2 minutes or 40; learners cannot plan a session or feel steady progress.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (taxi / app rides) — taxi is only a noun at 2.6. No Uber/Cabify/remis, no '¿me llevás a…?', '¿cuánto sale hasta…?', 'dejame acá', 'en la esquina está bien'. → Add to the transport unit above or to 3.9 segui-derecho: taxi/Uber phrases. _(Visitors take taxis and app cars from day one.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (money slang) — mango (3.12), guita (7.21), garpar (7.22) are taught, but never 'luca' (1,000) or 'palo' (million), 'gamba' (100); nor dólar blue / cambio / 'cambiar dólares' / cueva. → Add 'luca, lucas, palo' to 3.13 me-cobras (numbers in thousands) and 'dólar blue, cambiar dólares, ¿a cuánto está?' to 8.11 en-cuotas. _(Prices are said in lucas every day; visitors must change money on arrival.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (café orders) — 1.1-1.2 teach café, té, licuado; never cortado, café con leche, lágrima, 'para llevar / para tomar acá', 'con medialunas', 'chico/mediano/grande' for a coffee. → Add cortado, café con leche, lágrima, para llevar, para tomar acá to 1.1/1.2. _(The first unit is 'Order at a café' but lacks the words on every café menu.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (drinks and nightlife) — Bar vocabulary stops at cerveza (1.2) and vino (3.23). No trago, fernet (con coca), vino tinto/blanco, pinta, 'otra ronda', 'estoy en pedo', resaca, 'salimos de joda' until joda at 15.17. → Add a B1 unit 'A night out': previa, trago, fernet, birra, pinta, tinto, boliche, estoy en pedo, resaca, 'pintó salir'. Move birra here from 14.17. _(Going out is where learners actually meet locals; fernet is as iconic as mate.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (food restrictions) — Only vegetariano (5.10) and alergia (4.14). No vegano, celíaco / sin TACC, 'soy alérgico a…', 'sin gluten', '¿tiene carne / lácteos?', 'no como…'. → Add to 5.9 en-el-restaurante: soy alérgico/a a…, soy celíaco/a, sin TACC, vegano/a, ¿esto tiene…? _(Health-critical for some learners and printed on every Argentine package ('sin TACC').)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (basic clothes and colours) — 3.10-3.11 miss everyday items: medias, jean, pulóver/sweater, bufanda, malla, ropa interior, botas; colours rosa, naranja, violeta, celeste. Yet they teach 42+25 forms. → Swap some gender/plural duplicates in 3.10-3.11 for: jean, medias, pulóver, malla, botas; celeste, rosa, naranja, violeta. _(Celeste is the national colour; jean and medias are more common than pollera or gorra.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (body, face, looks) — Body parts in 4.13-4.14 skip pelo, cara, nariz, boca, dientes, cuello, estómago, pecho, piel; 2.2 describes people without pelo or ojos (rubio/morocho only). → Add pelo, cara, nariz, boca, dientes, estómago to 4.13/4.14, and 'tiene el pelo largo/corto, ojos claros, barba' to 2.2. _(Needed at the doctor, the hairdresser and to describe anyone.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (home objects) — Home units 2.22-2.23 and 5.22 have no toalla, sábanas, almohada, frazada, jabón, papel higiénico, shampoo, microondas, horno, hornalla, estufa, lamparita. → Add a short A2 unit or extend 2.23 mi-casa / 5.22 el-depto-nuevo with these household items. _(First things you ask a host or landlord for; also needed at the supermarket.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (renting: deposit, bills) — Renting is spread thin: alquiler/dueño/inmobiliaria 5.22, contrato/garantía 11.1, expensas 13.13. Never depósito, 'mes de adelanto', amoblado, 'incluye expensas', 'servicios incluidos', comisión (inmobiliaria). → Build one A2.3/B1.1 unit 'Rent a place': depósito, garantía, contrato, expensas, amoblado, ¿incluye los servicios?, ¿aceptan mascotas?, alquiler temporario. _(The learner who moves to Argentina needs this in month one, as one block.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (bureaucracy for foreigners) — 10.21-10.22 cover DNI, pasaporte, Migraciones, residencia. Missing: CUIL/CUIT, monotributo, factura (invoice), ARCA/AFIP, 'precaria', 'turno online', 'apostillado', 'antecedentes penales'. → Add CUIL, CUIT, monotributo, factura, precaria, antecedentes, apostilla to 10.22 migraciones or a new unit 'Work legally'. _(Anyone living or working in Argentina meets these words within weeks.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (congratulations, birthday, love) — 'Feliz cumple' is not in any word list (birthday unit 3.22 has cumple, regalo). 'Felicitaciones' first at 15.26. 'Te quiero', 'te amo', 'me gustás' never appear, even in 6.17-6.18. → Add ¡feliz cumple!, ¡felicitaciones!, ¡felicidades! to 3.22; te quiero, te amo, me gustás, me encantás to 6.17/6.18. _(Core social formulas; the love units teach 'mintió' and 'ex' but not 'te quiero'.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (quantity words) — No bastante, demasiado, suficiente, 'un poco de', 'una banda / una bocha', tremendo; 'muy' first at 3.10; 'tal vez' never (only quizás, capaz). → Add bastante, demasiado, un poco (de) to 2.8-2.9 with medio; 'una banda', 'tremendo' to a lunfardo unit. _(Among the 200 most frequent words of spoken Spanish.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (ordinals, floors, dates) — Only 'primero' (4.9) and 'último' (3.20). No segundo, tercero, cuarto (as ordinal), 'tercer piso', nor saying a date: '¿qué fecha es?', 'el 3 de marzo'. 'fecha' first at 15.2. → Add primer/segundo/tercer… piso to 2.22 mi-edificio, and '¿qué fecha es hoy?', 'el 25 de mayo', years to 3.20 en-febrero. _(Addresses (4° B), appointments and forms all need ordinals and dates.)_
- **medium** `missing` course-wide (frequent porteño words) — Not taught anywhere: zafar, nomás (ahí nomás, pasá nomás), 'ya está', lío, boludez, pegar onda, 'pintó', capo/crack, 'una masa', 'mal' as intensifier ('me gustó mal'), denso, 'nah', tremendo, colgar (te colgaste), 'qué hacés' as greeting is covered. → Add zafar, ya está, lío, boludez, nomás, capo, pintó, 'mal' (intensifier) across 7.21-7.22 and 8.25-8.26. _(All are heard daily; several are more common than berreta, chanta or macanudo, which are taught.)_
- **medium** `level` 2.15 me-traes-un-cafe — quiero/querés first at 2.15 (unit 38); puedo/podés at 3.5 (unit 51); 'muy' at 3.10; 'ahora', 'ya', 'todavía' at 3.23; 'baño' at 2.23. → Bring quiero, puedo, muy, ahora and '¿dónde está el baño?' into Section 1 as fixed phrases, before the nationality and family units. _(Core high-frequency words arrive after 22 nationalities and 17 family terms.)_
- **medium** `level` 1.16 de-todos-lados — 22 nationality forms and 102 sentences at A1.1 (brasileño… venezolana, paraguayo, peruana, estadounidense), right after 10 more in 1.15. → Keep 6-8 nationalities in A1.1; move the rest to an optional word pack. _(Too much low-value vocabulary before the learner can ask a price or say 'I want'.)_
- **medium** `level` 12.17 acabo-de — 'acabo de' [C1.1], diminutives 'un ratito, cafecito, poquito' at 14.9 [C1.3], 'lo que pasa es que' at 14.11 [C1.3], 'deberías' at 11.5 [B2.2], 'aunque' at 10.3 [B2.1]. → Move acabar de and diminutives to A2; deberías, aunque, lo que pasa es que to B1. _(These are heard daily and are simple; the CEFR labels on Sections 10-15 are inflated.)_
- **medium** `level` 14.17 ese-chabon — birra, mina, chabón, groso, zarpado, bardo, bajón, al pedo, cana first at 14.17-14.18 [C1.3]; pucho at 12.18; trucho at 13.12; joda at 15.17; 'al toque' at 12.26. → Move birra, chabón, mina, bajón, al pedo, joda, al toque, pucho into the B1 lunfardo block (7.21-7.22) or earlier. _(This is the slang heard in the first week; berreta and chanta (B1) are rarer.)_
- **medium** `level` 13.1 hay-paro — paro, corte, piquete, marcha first at 13.1 [C1.2]. → Move a slim version to B1 (near 8.9 manejar-en-baires or the new transport unit). _(Strikes and road cuts change plans weekly in Buenos Aires; needed long before C1.)_
- **medium** `level` 15.17 me-estas-cargando — chiste, gracioso, broma, 'en joda', '¿me estás cargando?' first at 15.17-15.18 [C1.4]; 'reír, llorar, canción' at 14.19 [C1.3]; tango, guitarra, cantante at 13.19-13.20 [C1.2]. → Move joking and laughing to B1; music words to A2 (3.17 que-te-gusta-hacer). _(Humour is the core of porteño social life; these are simple words placed at the end.)_
- **medium** `level` 9.17 el-cajero — transferencia, alias, QR, comprobante first at 9.17-9.18 [B1.3]; cuotas, débito, crédito at 8.11-8.12 [B1.2]. → Add 'te transfiero', alias, QR, '¿en cuotas?', débito/crédito to 3.13 me-cobras or an A2 unit. _(Paying by transfer or QR happens at every kiosco; cashiers ask 'débito o crédito' on day one.)_
- **medium** `not_relevant?` 13.5 las-elecciones / 13.6 el-cuarto-oscuro — Two units on voting: padrón, cuarto oscuro, boleta, urna, balotaje, justificar, encuesta. → Cut to one unit about talking politics (gobierno, elecciones, votar, 'no me meto'), or replace with a missing topic. Also check 'cuarto oscuro' against the 2025 single paper ballot. _(Most learners cannot vote; national elections moved to a single ballot, so 'cuarto oscuro' may be dated.)_
- **medium** `not_relevant` 13.3 fue-construido / 13.4 fue-clausurado — Passive news vocabulary: construido, inaugurado, clausurado, rescatados, trasladado, heridos, detenidos. → Shrink to one reading-only unit; give the slot to emergencies or swearing. _(Headline passive is for reading, not for talking like a local; two units is too much.)_
- **medium** `not_relevant` 15.13 mis-abuelos-italianos / 15.14 se-instalaron-en-la-boca — 'Tell where your family came from': bisabuelo, conventillo, gallego, ciudadanía, 'llegaron en barco', plus two practice units that reuse it. → Reframe as culture ('why Argentines say tano/gallego') in one unit, or move to culture cards. _(This is an Argentine's family story, not the foreign learner's; they will never say these lines.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` 9.9 el-partido / 13.17 de-que-cuadro-sos — Football is taught three times: 4.5-4.6 (cancha, partido, equipo, ganamos), 9.9-9.10 (hincha, gol, penal, campeón), 13.17-13.18 (cuadro, hincho, hinchada, socio). → Merge 13.17-13.18 into the B1 block; '¿de qué cuadro sos?' is a first-week question. _(Same topic and word family (hincha/hincho/hinchada) split across three sections.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` 8.13 dicen-que … 13.9 segun-el-diario — Hearsay/reported speech appears in six blocks: 8.13-8.14, 8.21-8.22, 9.25-9.26, 11.9-11.10, 12.1-12.4, 13.9-13.10. → Merge 8.13-8.14 with 13.9-13.10 (dicen que / según / al parecer) and 8.21-8.22 with 11.9-11.10. _('Someone said that…' is re-taught every section; scenarios blur together.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` 7.13 te-recomiendo / 8.1 yo-que-vos / 11.5 deberias — Advice is taught in three separate blocks of two units each (te recomiendo/te aconsejo, yo que vos/en tu lugar, deberías/estaría bueno), each with two practice units. → Teach 'deberías' with 'yo que vos' in Section 8 and free the Section 11 slot. _(Same function three times; the simplest form (deberías) comes last.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` 10.5 llevo-dos-anos / 12.17 acabo-de — 'dejar de' and 'volver a' are new grammar at 10.5-10.6 and again at 12.17-12.18; 'dejé de fumar' is the example both times (fumar 10.5, fumo/pucho 12.18). → Teach dejar de / volver a once; make 12.17-12.18 only acabar de / soler / ponerse a. _(The same two structures and the same smoking example are taught as new twice.)_
- **medium** `experience` 3.10 ropa-y-colores — 42 new word forms in one A1.3 unit (also 2.11: 37, 3.1/3.15/3.23: 35, 2.2/2.10/3.5: 34), against 2-5 in units like 1.5, 14.1, 14.21, 8.13. → Cap new words at about 12-15 lemmas per unit; split the big A1 units in two. _(A1 learners get the heaviest vocabulary loads of the whole course.)_
- **medium** `experience` 3.5 queres-podes-vas — Introduces 15 infinitives at once (ir, salir, hablar, tener, ser, hacer, comer, vivir, aprender, estar, escribir, ver, entender, abrir, saber) plus poder, ir and salir conjugations; 144 sentences, 1 tip. → Split into 'puedo / podés' and 'voy / vas', and bring infinitives in with tener que (2.17). _(Three irregular verbs and the infinitive concept in one unit with a single tip.)_
- **medium** `experience` 3.1 la-hora — One unit teaches telling the time, parts of the day, 7 weekdays and numbers 21-100 (35 words, 110 sentences). → Split: numbers 21-100 (with prices), then time, then days of the week. _(Three separate survival topics squeezed into a single unit.)_
- **medium** `experience` sections 10-15 (CEFR labels) — Sections 12-15 are tagged C1 but hold topics like ordering at the parrilla, mate, weddings, a trip south, 'acabo de', diminutives. → Either relabel honestly (the course ends near B2) or move simple topics down and fill C1 with truly advanced language. _('C1' overpromises; a learner at that label expects more than '¿Me pasás un choripán?')_
- **low** `missing` course-wide (flirting and dating) — 6.17-6.18 cover going out and breaking up, but not the Argentine verbs: chapar, levantar(se a alguien), tirar onda, histeriquear, 'hay onda', 'estamos saliendo' exists. → Add chapar, tirar onda, hay onda, levante to 6.17 or to a lunfardo unit. _(Learners asked for 'socialising and dating like a local'; current words are textbook-neutral.)_
- **low** `missing` course-wide (connectors) — Never listed: sino, durante, hacia, 'en vez de', 'a propósito', 'ya que', 'apenas' as 'hardly', 'ni… ni'. 'aunque' first at 10.3 [B2.1]. → Add sino / ni… ni / en vez de / durante to B1 units (e.g. 9.13 de-acuerdo, 8.25 ponele). _('No es caro, sino barato' and 'durante' are needed well before C1.)_
- **low** `missing` course-wide (delivery and online buying) — No pedir delivery, pedido, 'retiro en el local', Mercado Libre / Mercado Pago, 'te lo mando por moto', seguimiento. 'envío' only on shop signs at 11.14. → Add to 9.18 pasame-el-alias or 6.9 el-celu: pedir delivery, pedido, envío, Mercado Pago, 'pago con QR'. _(How people in Buenos Aires actually buy food and things today.)_
- **low** `missing` course-wide (services: hairdresser, laundry, gym) — peluquería, lavadero, gimnasio appear only as place names (3.4, 3.18). No 'cortar el pelo', 'un poco más corto', 'lavar y secar', cuota del gimnasio. → Add one A2/B1 unit 'Errands': cortarme el pelo, corto/largo, lavar la ropa, ¿para cuándo está?, anotarme en el gimnasio. _(Routine errands for someone living there; currently only the shop names are known.)_
- **low** `level` 1.18 tios-y-primos — cuñado, suegro, suegra, sobrino, nieto, nieta at A1.1 unit 18, before numbers, 'hay', 'quiero' or 'dónde'. → Move in-laws and grandchildren to A2 (e.g. 5.14 en-lo-de-la-abuela); keep tío/primo. _(In-law words are rare for a beginner; survival words wait behind them.)_
- **low** `level` 10.21 el-tramite — DNI and pasaporte first at 10.21 [B2.1]; trámite at 6.3, turno at 4.13. → Introduce DNI and pasaporte at 6.4 hay-que-sacar-turno, which already has fotocopia and firmar. _(6.4 is the paperwork unit but lacks the two documents everyone asks for.)_
- **low** `experience` 6.9 el-celu — 'SUBE' is listed as a new word in the phone unit 'Deal with your phone' (6.9), not in a transport unit. → Teach SUBE with colectivo/subte (2.5) or the new transport unit. _(The transport card is hidden in a tech unit, 150 units after the bus is introduced.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` 5.25 las-figuritas — calesita, barrilete, álbum, figuritas, golosinas, guardapolvo (5.2) as active vocabulary for 'your' childhood. → Keep as listening/culture; teach neutral childhood words the learner can use about their own past. _(The learner did not grow up in Argentina; these memories are not theirs to tell.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` 8.9 manejar-en-baires / 8.10 la-ruta — Two driving units: General Paz, peaje, cochera, registro, multa, choqué. → Keep one driving unit; use the other for public transport and taxis. _(Most visitors and new residents do not drive in Buenos Aires; transport by bus has no unit.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` 14.13 como-dice-el-dicho / 14.14 cada-loco-con-su-tema — 12 proverbs taught as 'words', e.g. 'el que se quema con leche, ve una vaca y llora', 'más vale pájaro en mano que cien volando'. → Keep the 4-5 most used (más vale tarde que nunca, el que no llora no mama, hablando del rey de Roma); drop the rest. _(Long proverbs are rarely said in full and take two units plus two practice units.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` 15.1 la-entrega – 15.4 se-merece-el-ascenso — Section 'Like a local' opens with four office units: plazo, presupuesto, borrador, evaluación, gerente, objetivos. → Move the office block to Section 12 with the work emails; open Section 15 with local-life topics. _(Corporate vocabulary does not fit a section titled 'Like a local'.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` 2.20 vendo-diarios — 'Vendo diarios en el negocio de mi viejo'; words diario, diarios, revista, revistas, mail, mails. → Use a more current barrio scene for -er/-ir verbs (vender, abrir, recibir) – e.g. a kiosco or verdulería. _(Selling newspapers and magazines is a dated scenario for an adult learner.)_
- **low** `repetitive` 7.9 no-creo / 9.13 de-acuerdo / 10.19 por-un-lado / 10.25 te-doy-la-razon — Opinions and agreeing: 7.9-7.10, 9.13-9.14, 10.19-10.20, 10.25-10.26 – eight units; Section 10 has two debate blocks. → Fold 10.25-10.26 into 9.13-9.14 or 10.19-10.20. _(Four near-identical 'give your opinion' blocks while everyday topics are missing.)_
- **low** `repetitive` 6.25 sos-un-genio / 7.25 saludos-a-tu-vieja / 15.25 gracias-por-todo — Closing blocks overlap: thanking (6.25-6.26), goodbyes (7.25-7.26), and thanks + goodbye again (15.25). → Fine as section endings, but give 7.26 new content; 'Cuidate mucho' adds only 5 words. _(7.25 and 7.26 are the same function with almost no new language.)_
- **low** `repetitive` 4.9 el-finde / 4.15 practica-el-finde — Identical summary phrases: 4.9 & 4.15 '¿Qué hiciste el finde?'; 6.9 & 6.15 'Me quedé sin batería'; 8.13 & 8.15 'Dicen que va a llover'; 7.2 & 7.8 'Necesito que me ayudes'; 5.11 & 5.15 'Nos vemos tipo ocho'. → Give each practice unit its own phrase. _(On the path two cards a few steps apart show the same sentence and look like a bug.)_
- **low** `experience` course-wide (summary phrase style) — Most summaries are sayable phrases ('¿Cuánto sale?'), but some are labels or verb lists: 3.1 'La hora', 3.3 'El barrio', 3.10 'Ropa y colores', 3.15 'La rutina', 3.19 'Clima', 3.23 'Ahora y planes', 2.19 'Comés, vivís', 3.5 'Querés, podés, vas', 1.17 'Mi familia', 2.23 'Mi casa'. → Replace with a real phrase: '¿Qué hora es?', 'Está a dos cuadras', 'Me gusta esa remera', 'Me levanto a las siete', 'Hace calor', 'Estoy llegando'. _(Inconsistent card style; labels tell the learner nothing they will say.)_
- **low** `experience` course-wide (title style) — Vague 'part two' titles: 15.20 'Share the other big news', 14.17 'More lunfardo', 12.14 'Use more porteño la idioms', 7.26 'Say goodbye properly', 6.26 'Thank someone properly'. Near-synonym titles: 7.21 'Talk like a porteño', 8.25 'Talk like you're from here', 8.26 'Sound porteño', 14.18 'Talk like the barrio'. → Name each by its content: 15.20 'Graduations, retirements and funerals'; 8.25 'Hedge with ponele and digamos'; 8.26 'Say just in case'. _(Titles do not say what the unit teaches, and four of them are interchangeable.)_
- **low** `experience` 6.7 practica-los-mandados — Mixed English spelling: 'favors' (6.7), 'rumors' (13.15) vs 'favours' (6.1, 6.8, 7.8), 'colours' (3.10). → Pick one variety (the course mostly uses UK: favours, colours, rumours) and apply everywhere. _(Two adjacent titles spell the same word differently.)_
- **low** `experience?` 12.5 usted — Slugs that contradict house rules or content: 12.5 slug 'usted' (unit teaches polite vos); 9.7 slug 'practica-se-me-olvido' (house form is 'se me pasó'); 7.19 slug 'no-se' with phrase 'Ni idea'. → Rename slugs if they are ever shown or used in analytics: 'disculpa-que-te-moleste', 'practica-se-me-paso'. _(Stale slugs hint that old content (usted, se me olvidó) may linger inside those units.)_
- **low** `experience?` 3.21 practica-el-clima — Practice units list stray 'new' words already taught: 3.21 cocina, 5.24 casa, 7.16 llena, 11.16 trabajo, 12.8 me siento, 12.15 demora. → Check these six word tags; they look like homograph mis-tags (cocina = kitchen/cooks) rather than new words. _(Practice units should have no new words; these will show as 'new' to the learner.)_
- **low** `experience` sections 4-15 (section titles) — Section titles name one grammar idea ('When I was a kid', 'If I were you') but each section also holds unrelated topics (restaurant, moving, bank, football). → Fine to keep, but add a one-line subtitle per section listing its real-life topics, e.g. 'A2.2 – eating out, meeting up, moving house'. _(A learner looking for 'the doctor' or 'the bank' cannot find it from section titles.)_
- **low** `experience` 15.26 ya-sos-de-aca — Final unit: 27 sentences, 6 words, and the Obelisco appears for the first time. It follows two 110+ sentence practice units and there is no course-wide final review. → Keep the warm ending, but add a short capstone (one unit mixing situations from all sections) before 15.25, and introduce Obelisco in the barrios unit (8.19). _(Nice emotional close, but thin; the course ends without checking what the learner can now do.)_

## Lessons: how the exercises work


### lesson-flow

- **high** `level` units mi-casa (A1.2) and ahora-y-planes (A1.3) — forms heladera, sillón, cama, cosa, cosas, pibes, vino, juntada, copado/copada, próximo/próxima, viste, boludo, quilombo — 15 published words have no teach slot anywhere, yet 313 drill slots in later units use them. First hits: el-barrio L9 #8 build "El depto tiene heladera, pero no tiene cama." (target heladera); ayer-labure L11 "¿Cuánto vino tomaste ayer?"; comi-y-sali L11 #5 gap "La juntada de hoy va a estar copada."; cenamos-afuera L11 "Los pibes hablaron de fútbol." → Add teach slots (teach → meaning → gap) for these 15 words in their home units (5 in mi-casa, 10 in ahora-y-planes) — each needs one more lesson — then re-run course:lessons --all so later drills stop being first contact. _(Learners must build and gap-fill words the course never introduced.)_
- **high** `experience` section-final units: en-el-kiosco, mi-casa, ahora-y-planes, contame, te-acordas, te-debo-una, cuidate, por-las-dudas, viste-lo-que-paso, que-opinas, ni-ahi, te-la-hago-corta, lo-bueno-de-vivir-aca, no-te-lo-tomes-a-mal, ya-sos-de-aca (59 lessons of kind checkpoint) — Lessons titled "Checkpoint 1…9" are drawn as trophy "Unit check" (home.tsx KIND_LABEL) and graded as a test needing 80% (practice.tsx kind unit_check), but they are ordinary teaching lessons: en-el-kiosco "Checkpoint 1" = TIP + TEACH kiosco, cuántas, empanada + meaning/gap/build. ahora-y-planes has 9 of them in a row. → Change these 59 lessons to kind "lesson" (titles "Lesson N") and give each of these units a real closing check: a recap slot with scope "section" + 3 builds, like every other unit has. _(New words are taught inside a pass/fail test; the section never gets a real final check.)_
- **high** `level` slang lessons of units 1–12 (un-cafe-por-favor L2, otro-cafe L3, hola-che, buen-dia L3, practica-hola L2, encantado…) — Unit 1 (learner knows 5 words: agua, por favor, medialuna, gracias, café) → slang "ahre", "al mango", "amigovio = friend with benefits" with example "Mañana renuncio y me voy a vivir a Bali, ahre." Unit 7 → "telo = love motel" («Como viven con los viejos, van a un telo.»). Unit 4 → "caer la ficha" («Recién hoy me cayó la ficha de que me mudo.»). → Start slang lessons only from A1.3/A2 (when the learner can read a sentence), and order words by usefulness (che, dale, re, laburo-type words first), not alphabetically inside a theme. Until then show at most one very common word with a 3–4 word example. _(Absolute beginners get rare slang with past-tense example sentences they cannot read.)_
- **high** `repetitive` every lesson of kind lesson/practice, all 15 sections — All 2,400 lessons follow two fixed templates. Teaching: [tip] · (teach · meaning · gap)×3 · build · build · build · review 2 · match. Practice: review 2 · gap ×3 · 4 recycled (gap/build/gap/build) · typed gap ×2 · the same 3 sentences as builds · match. The exercise mix is identical in A1.1 and C1.4 (lesson: teach 22% / meaning 22% / gap 21% / build 19%; practice: gap 36% / build 32–34% / typed 14–16%). → Vary the template by level: A1 as now; A2 add listening and typed gaps inside teaching lessons; B1+ replace "pick the meaning" with English→Spanish builds and typed full short sentences; B2/C1 add mini-dialogues (2–4 lines), reorder-the-conversation, and choose-the-best-reply. Also vary the order inside a level so lessons do not always end build·build·build·match. _(After a few units the learner can predict every screen; C1 feels like A1.)_
- **high** `level` whole course; e.g. practica-no-es-que (C1.3) L1–L4, te-aconsejo (B1.1) L6–L7 — Production is one typed word in a gap, only in practice lessons (2,270 of 32,736 slots = 7%; 0 typed slots in the 1,357 teaching lessons). No screen ever asks for a whole typed sentence or a free answer. C1.3 practice: gap "Ya me ___." → build "Ya me arrepiento." from tiles. → From A2: add 1–2 typed gaps to every teaching lesson. From B1: add "type this in Spanish" for sentences of ≤6 words (graded with es_alt + the existing accent/typo tolerance). From B2: make the unit check at least half typed. _(Tile-building is recognition; learners reach C1 without ever writing a sentence.)_
- **high** `level` practice lessons at B2–C1, e.g. practica-no-es-que (C1.3), practica-me-mori-de-risa (C1.3) — Lessons always take the shortest sentences first. Own sentences in practice lessons average 4.5 words at C1 (pool average 5.8). C1.3 drills: "Sí, me arrepiento." "Ya me arrepiento." "Nunca me arrepentí." "Tendría que haber ido." / "Tendrías que haber ido." "Necesito guita." "No tengo guita." "¡Estoy manija!" "¿Estás manija?" → Pick by level: from B1 skip sentences under 5 words for gaps and builds, prefer two-clause sentences, and use the longest sayable ones in practice lessons instead of only in the last build. _(Difficulty does not grow: C1 drills are three-word sentences, easier than A2 ones.)_
- **high** `experience` placement test (span = units.slice(0, 15)) and jump tests (canJumpTo: span ≤ 15 units, pass with ≤1 miss in 30) — The onboarding placement test only samples the first 15 units (all A1.1), so the best result is "start at unit 16 of 381". After that a learner can only jump 15 units at a time, each jump a 30-question test allowing one mistake. A real B1 speaker needs about 10 tests to reach section 7. → Make placement adaptive across the whole course: 2 questions from one unit per section (15 sections), binary-search style, then refine inside the section where they fail. Allow 3 misses in a 30-question jump. _(Intermediate learners are sent back to "Un café, por favor" and will leave.)_
- **medium** `experience` every slang and culture lesson on the path (215 + 84) — Slang and culture are dealt out by a fixed list, 3 words/1 class per unit, with no link to the unit: "Order at a café" gets ahre/al mango/amigovio; "Say hello and goodbye" (buen-dia) gets ortiba/boludez/caer la ficha + a class on dulce de leche; "Talk to someone as vos" gets batero (drummer)/calentarse/bochar + football clubs; "Order something to eat" gets the asado class. → Pick each unit's slang and culture class by topic: café units → mate, medialunas/facturas, "cortado"; greetings → "che", "¿qué onda?", el beso class; vos unit → the "vos-sos-vos" class (now at unit 8); food units → asado/comida classes. Keep the mechanical order only as a fallback. _(Extras feel random; they interrupt the unit instead of deepening it.)_
- **medium** `experience` units after practica-el-finde (culture ends, unit 84 of 381) and after practica-tenes-razon (slang ends, unit 215) — Culture lessons exist only in the first 84 units (A1.1–A2.1) and slang lessons only in the first 215; from B2.1 on, units are only practice/lesson · speak · unit check. → Spread the 84 culture classes and 645 slang words over all 381 units (e.g. culture every 4–5 units, slang 2 words per unit) and move history/regional classes to B1+, where learners can discuss them. _(Beginners get all the culture while advanced learners, who could use it best, get none.)_
- **medium** `not_relevant` practica-no-es-que (C1.3) — title "Practice: excuses, what-ifs and regrets", grammar repaso.no-es-que / condicional-mixto — The 4 practice lessons never drill "no es que…" or a mixed conditional from this unit: all 12 own gaps/builds are "me arrepiento / me arrepentí / tendría(s) que haber + participle / hay que aprovechar". "No es que" appears only in the L1 tip; hubiera only in recycled sentences and the unit check. → For practice units, choose sentences per reviewed structure (one third "No es que no quiera, es que no puedo"-type, one third "Si hubiera…, ahora…", one third regrets) instead of the 12 shortest. _(The unit does not practise two of the three things its title promises.)_
- **medium** `level` C1 practice lessons, e.g. practica-no-es-que L3 #5, L4 #7–8; practica-me-mori-de-risa L1 #7–8, L3 #7, L4 #5 — Recycled slots in C1 bring back beginner sentences: "¡Buen día! —Buenas, ¿qué onda?", "Lucía es casada y su marido es chileno.", "¿Anteojos blancos? ¡Qué lindos!", "Cruzá la avenida y doblá a la derecha.", "Seguí derecho y doblá en la avenida.", "Cruzá la plaza y seguí derecho." (3 direction sentences in one unit). 290 of 1,164 recycled C1 slots come from A1/A2. → Limit recycling to the previous 2–3 CEFR bands (C1 recycles B1–C1), and bring old words back inside new, level-appropriate sentences instead of the original A1 sentence. _(A C1 learner gap-filling "Buen día" feels the course is not following their level.)_
- **medium** `tip_unclear` 168 of 523 tips in teaching lessons; e.g. el-barrio L1, te-aconsejo L1–L2, buen-dia L2, tengo-hambre L1, altos-y-morochos L1 — Tips are attached by position (tip 1 → lesson 1, tip 2 → lesson 2), not by content. el-barrio L1 opens with "al lado de / enfrente de / atrás de / entre" but teaches barrio, verdulería, panadería; those words come in L5–L6. te-aconsejo L1 opens with "Advice for us… salgamos" but salgamos is taught in L4. buen-dia L2 tip "Gracias, de nada / claro / joya" — taught in L4 and L6. → Give each tip a lesson (or a form) it belongs to and place it directly before the first teach slot of the words it explains. _(The explanation arrives lessons before (or after) the words it explains, so it is forgotten or confusing.)_
- **medium** `tip_unclear` 145 of 146 units with a "Grammar practice" lesson; e.g. te-aconsejo (B1.1) L5 — The pattern table for the unit's grammar ("Te aconsejo que **lleves** efectivo / Conviene que **tomes** el subte…") is shown only at the start of Grammar practice (L5), after three lessons that already drilled lleves, tomes, busques, cambies, uses, reserves, salgamos with no explanation of the subjunctive. → Show the grammar table as the first slot of the unit's Lesson 1 (short version), and again in Grammar practice. _(Learners drill a new verb form for three lessons before being told what it is.)_
- **medium** `weird` la-hora L12–L14 (sesenta, ochenta, noventa); otro-cafe L6 (comida); el-barrio L8 (muchas); es-enfermera L8 (ayudar); cien-gramos-de-jamon L1 (gramo); laburo-nuevo L7 (mala); el-partido L1 (gano); si-hubieramos-salido L4 (demorada); estas-cambiado L4 (desaparecieron); tendria-que-haber L2 (aprovechar) — 12 words are taught and then never appear in the rest of the lesson. la-hora L13: TEACH ochenta → next screens "¿Qué hacés hoy?", "¿Qué hacés mañana?", "La reunión es el martes veintidós a las diez." la-hora L14: TEACH noventa, TEACH cien back to back, then unrelated sentences. → Write 2 sentences for each of these words (e.g. "Mi abuela tiene ochenta años.", "Sale noventa pesos.") and place meaning + gap right after the teach slot; fill the rest of la-hora L13–L14 with number sentences. _(A word shown once on a card and not used is not learned; the lesson feels broken.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` vos-y-sos L1 (c03b87c0); also un-cafe-por-favor L3–L4, como-te-llamas L1 and L3, de-donde-sos L1, hola-che L8, el-y-ella L3 — vos-y-sos L1 teaches one word (vos) and shows "Todo bien, ¿y vos?" four times (meaning #3, gap #5, build #8, listen #9) and "Soy Sofi. ¿Y vos?" three times, in 9 exercise screens. 11 lessons repeat a sentence 3+ times. → Add 3–4 more short sentences per early unit ("¿Y vos, Juan?", "Yo café, ¿y vos?", "Vos primero.") so no sentence appears more than twice in a lesson. _(The learner answers from memory of the previous screen, not from knowing the word.)_
- **medium** `experience` A1.3 units, e.g. ropa-y-colores (21 lessons: 16 teaching lessons before the first practice), que-haces (20), la-hora (17) — New words per unit: A1.1 10 · A1.2 17 · A1.3 19 · A2.1 13 · B1 7 · C1 7.5. The beginner sections are the densest: ropa-y-colores teaches 42 words in 16 lessons in a row, with one practice lesson at the very end. → Split A1.2/A1.3 units over 12 lessons into two units (clothes / colours; hours / days), and put a practice lesson after every 3–4 teaching lessons instead of all at the end. _(The vocabulary load peaks exactly where learners are weakest; long units feel endless.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` 81 practice-only units (3 per A1 section, 6 per section from A2.1), e.g. practica-que-hiciste #75 and practica-como-estuvo #76 back to back — From A2 on, 6 of every 26 units (23%) are "Practice:" units of 4 identical practice lessons + speak + check, with nothing new: no new word, no story, no new situation. Two of them are adjacent in A2.1 (units 75 and 76). → Make each review unit different from normal practice: a short story/dialogue to read and answer, a role-play, or a "real life" task (read a WhatsApp chat, a menu, a sign). Never place two review units in a row. _(A quarter of the course is the same drill again; this is where learners quit.)_
- **medium** `missing` hola-che L5 "At the café" — the only story in the course — The course has one story lesson (10 lines) and it is hidden from the path. Only 92 of 13,129 lesson sentences are two-line exchanges ("—… —…"). Everything else is isolated sentences with no speaker, no situation and no follow-up. → Finish the story player and add one short dialogue per unit (6–10 lines using the unit's words, with 2–3 comprehension questions). The sentences already written per unit can be chained into these. _(Learners never see a conversation, the thing the course promises to teach.)_
- **medium** `level` speak lesson of early units, e.g. un-cafe-por-favor L7, otro-cafe L8, buen-dia L8 — Every unit, including unit 1, ends with a live chat with Pancho pitched at band "A1": "a foreigner who has studied a few weeks… soy, tengo, querés, vivís, hay, me gusta". The unit-1 learner knows 8 nouns plus por favor/gracias and no verb (soy arrives in unit 3, querés much later). The lesson cannot be skipped: the unit check stays locked behind it. → For A1.1 make the speak lesson a scripted exchange limited to the words taught so far (Pancho: "¿Café o mate?" → learner says/builds "Un café, por favor."). Open free chat from A1.3. Add "Not now" so the path continues and the chat stays available. _(A beginner with eight words is pushed into free conversation and cannot move on without it.)_
- **medium** `missing` slang lessons on the path (215) — The 645 slang words taught in path slang lessons are played once ("nothing is scheduled") and never return: they are excluded from review slots, recaps, unit checks and course sentences. → Add slang words the learner has seen to the SM-2 schedule (or at least to "My words" and to the review slots), and reuse them in later unit sentences. _(Slang seen once in three screens is forgotten; it is the content learners came for.)_
- **medium** `missing` whole course (19 sentence_listen slots, all in the first 6 units) — Outside six A1.1 units there is no listening exercise and no speaking exercise inside lessons; the only audio is the separate chat with Pancho. → Once audio is recorded: add 2 listening screens per lesson (hear → pick meaning at A1, hear → type at B1+) and one "say it" screen per practice lesson. _(A course for talking like a local is currently a silent reading-and-tapping course.)_
- **low** `experience?` all 381 speak lessons — The unit scene (setting, goals, key phrases, opener) is written by the model the first time any learner opens it and then served to everyone; nobody reviews it. → Pre-generate all unit scenes, review them like other content (check key phrases use only taught words), and store them before learners reach them. _(Unreviewed generated text reaches learners in a course whose selling point is correct Argentine Spanish.)_
- **low** `repetitive` review lessons ("Unit check"), e.g. un-cafe-por-favor L8, el-barrio L11 — Every unit check is recap N + the 3 longest sentences as tile builds — the same sentences already built in the lessons (un-cafe-por-favor L8 builds dab86036, f19018ed, 1faa79cc, built before in L1 and L4; el-barrio L11 repeats the builds of L1, L5, L8). → Use sentences not yet shown in the unit for the check (half of the 26,411 published sentences are never placed in a lesson), and mix modes: one typed gap, one listening when audio exists, one build. _(A check that repeats screens already seen measures short-term memory, not learning.)_
- **low** `experience?` gradeWord — accent step; e.g. practica-que-hiciste L6 #9 typed gap "Anoche ___ tarde." (laburé) — A typed answer without its accent is accepted (with a note) even when the accent is the grammar being tested: "laburo" for "laburé", "tomas" for "tomás". The tip of the same unit says "only the stress moves: la-BU-ro is now, la-bu-RÉ is done". → Keep forgiving accents in general, but when the unaccented spelling is another real form of the same verb (laburo/laburé, tomas/tomás, hablo/habló) mark it wrong, or accept once and re-ask the item. _(The one contrast the unit teaches can be ignored and still score 100%.)_

## Argentine words (slang packs)


### slang-overview

- **high** `missing` plata — (not in the list) → Add `plata = money` (plata theme, L1). Ex: "No tengo plata." = I don't have money. _(The everyday word for money; the theme is even named after it. Only guita is there.)_
- **high** `missing` laburar — (not in the list) → Add `laburar = to work` (verbos, L1). Ex: "Mañana laburo todo el día." = I work all day tomorrow. _(laburo and laburante are cards but the verb, used every day, is not.)_
- **high** `missing` capaz — (not in the list) → Add `capaz = maybe` (charla, L1). Ex: "Capaz voy más tarde." = Maybe I'll go later. _(Porteños say capaz far more than quizás; learners hear it daily.)_
- **high** `missing` o sea — (not in the list) → Add `o sea = I mean` (charla, L1, Filler). Ex: "O sea, no es tan caro." = I mean, it's not that expensive. _(Top filler in Buenos Aires speech; tipo, viste and ponele are in, this is not.)_
- **high** `missing` qué hacés — (not in the list) → Add `qué hacés = hi, how are you?` (charla, L1, Greeting, not a real question). Ex: "¡Qué hacés, Juan! ¿Todo bien?" _(Most common greeting; learners answer it literally ('what are you doing').)_
- **high** `missing` chau — (not in the list) → Add `chau = bye` (charla, L1). Ex: "Chau, nos vemos mañana." = Bye, see you tomorrow. _(Nobody says adiós in Buenos Aires; chau is the goodbye.)_
- **high** `missing` finde — (not in the list) → Add `finde = weekend` (charla, L1). Ex: "¿Qué hacés el finde?" = What are you doing this weekend? _(Used in every plan and every WhatsApp chat.)_
- **high** `missing` joder — (not in the list) → Add `joder = to kid; to bother` (verbos, L1) with `dejate de joder` = stop messing around / no way. Ex: "¿Me estás jodiendo?" = Are you kidding me? _(Only the noun joda is there; the verb is heard all day.)_
- **high** `missing` pará — (not in the list) → Add `pará = wait, hold on` (charla, L1). Ex: "Pará, pará, ¿qué dijiste?" = Wait, what did you say? _(Extremely common; and the pararse card says "Not 'to stop'", which confuses this.)_
- **high** `missing` tranqui — (not in the list) → Add `tranqui = relaxed; no worries` (charla, L1). Ex: "Tranqui, no pasa nada." = Relax, it's fine. _(The list has the rarer `tranca` but not tranqui, which everybody says.)_
- **high** `missing` viejo / mis viejos — (not in the list) → Add `viejo = dad` and `mis viejos = my parents` (gente, L1). Ex: "Vivo con mis viejos." = I live with my parents. _(Only vieja = mom is there; mis viejos is the normal way to say 'my parents'.)_
- **high** `missing` recién — (not in the list) → Add `recién = just now` (charla, L1). Ex: "Recién llego." = I just got here. _(Very Argentine use; learners expect 'acabo de'.)_
- **high** `experience` whole list: pack order — Packs of 5 are dealt in alphabetical order inside each level (first charla pack: a full, ahre, al toque, alto, bárbaro) → Order cards inside each level by how common/useful they are (che, dale, re, posta, qué onda first), or group packs by small topic. _(Alphabetical packs put rare words before core ones and make every pack start with the same letter.)_
- **high** `experience` puteadas: boludo, gil, hacerse el boludo, en pedo, cagarse de risa — boludo = dude; idiot [puteadas, L1, vulgar] → Move boludo (friendly sense), gil, hacerse el boludo, boludear-family and cagarse de risa to open themes (charla/gente/expresiones), with a 'careful' flag. _(The single most heard Argentine word is hidden behind the adults-only theme.)_
- **medium** `missing` igual — (not in the list) → Add `igual = anyway, still` (charla, L1). Ex: "Llueve, pero voy igual." = It's raining, but I'm going anyway. _(Constant in speech and its meaning is not 'equal'.)_
- **medium** `missing` por las dudas — (not in the list) → Add `por las dudas = just in case` (expresiones, L1). Ex: "Llevá paraguas por las dudas." = Take an umbrella just in case. _(Daily Argentine phrase (neutral Spanish says por si acaso).)_
- **medium** `missing` ni idea — (not in the list) → Add `ni idea = no idea` (charla, L1). Ex: "—¿A qué hora abre? —Ni idea." _(One of the most common short answers.)_
- **medium** `missing` no te puedo creer — (not in the list) → Add `no te puedo creer = I can't believe it` (expresiones, L1). Ex: "¿Renunció? ¡No te puedo creer!" _(The standard reaction to any news; heard constantly.)_
- **medium** `missing` fijate — (not in the list) → Add `fijarse / fijate = to check, take a look` (verbos, L1). Ex: "Fijate si hay leche." = Check if there's milk. _(Very common everyday verb with a non-obvious meaning.)_
- **medium** `missing` celu — (not in the list) → Add `celu = cell phone` (casa or charla, L1). Ex: "Me quedé sin batería en el celu." = My phone died. _(Everyone says celu; neutral courses teach móvil/teléfono.)_
- **medium** `missing` afanar — (not in the list) → Add `afanar = to steal; to overcharge` (verbos, L1). Ex: "Me afanaron el celu en el bondi." = They stole my phone on the bus. _(The list has the rare `afanador` (L3) but not the very common verb.)_
- **medium** `missing` porro — (not in the list) → Add `porro = joint` (noche, L1). Ex: "Había olor a porro en la plaza." = The square smelled of weed. _(The real word for a joint; list has only pito/troncho/faso.)_
- **medium** `missing` denso — (not in the list) → Add `denso = annoying, intense person` (gente, L1). Ex: "No seas denso, ya te dije que no." = Don't be so annoying, I said no. _(Very common description of people; plomo is in, denso is not.)_
- **medium** `missing` romperla — (not in the list) → Add `romperla = to do something great` (expresiones, L1). Ex: "La rompiste en la entrevista." = You did great in the interview. _(Current everyday praise; meaning is the opposite of what a learner guesses.)_
- **medium** `missing` estar manija — (not in the list) → Add `manija = very excited, can't wait` (animo, L1). Ex: "Estoy re manija con el viaje." = I can't wait for the trip. _(Very current youth use; the list only has the older `dar manija`.)_
- **medium** `missing` trámite — (not in the list) → Add `trámite = paperwork, official errand` (ciudad, L1). Ex: "Tengo que hacer un trámite en el banco." _(Anyone living in Argentina does trámites every week.)_
- **medium** `missing` expensas — (not in the list) → Add `expensas = monthly building fees` (casa or plata, L1). Ex: "El alquiler no incluye las expensas." = Rent doesn't include building fees. _(Essential for renting an apartment; a real money surprise for foreigners.)_
- **medium** `missing` DNI — (not in the list) → Add `DNI = national ID card` (ciudad, L1). Ex: "¿Me decís tu DNI?" = Can you tell me your ID number? _(Asked for in shops, deliveries, buses and every form.)_
- **medium** `missing` prepaga — (not in the list) → Add `prepaga = private health plan` (plata, L1). Ex: "¿Tenés prepaga u obra social?" _(Paired with obra social (already a card) in every clinic.)_
- **medium** `missing` transferir / te transfiero — (not in the list) → Add `transferir = to pay by bank transfer` (plata, L1). Ex: "¿Te transfiero o te pago en efectivo?" = Shall I transfer or pay cash? _(How people pay each other and shops today (with Mercado Pago/QR); `alias` is there but not this.)_
- **medium** `missing` en blanco — (not in the list) → Add `en blanco = registered, legal (job, pay)` (plata, L1). Ex: "Por fin tengo un laburo en blanco." _(The pair of `en negro`, which is already a card.)_
- **medium** `missing` ajuste — (not in the list) → Add `ajuste = spending cuts` (politica, L1). Ex: "El ajuste lo pagan los jubilados." = Retired people pay for the cuts. _(Central word of current politics; also add `motosierra` (Milei's 'chainsaw' cuts) and `libertario`.)_
- **medium** `missing` piquete / marcha — (not in the list) → Add `piquete = road-block protest` and `marcha = protest march` (politica, L1). Ex: "Hay un piquete en la 9 de Julio, llego tarde." _(Daily traffic news; piquetero is a card but not the thing itself.)_
- **medium** `missing` cuadro — (not in the list) → Add `cuadro = football team (club)` (futbol, L1). Ex: "¿De qué cuadro sos?" = Which team do you support? _(The first question any Argentine asks a foreigner.)_
- **medium** `missing` la Selección — (not in the list) → Add `la Selección = the national team` (futbol, L1). Ex: "Hoy juega la Selección." = The national team plays today. _(The normal name; the list has only the nicknames Scaloneta/albiceleste.)_
