- **high** `missing` (new class: safety) — Safety is one card: 'The thief to know is the motochorro' (buenos-aires/vida-portena). → Add 'Street smarts': phone away near the curb, bag in front on the subte, the 'stain on your jacket' trick, areas that change at night, app or radio taxi at night, and the phrases locals use ('no te regales', 'está picante', '¡ojo!'). _(Safety is every newcomer's first question and gets one sentence.)_
- **high** `missing` (new class after democracia-y-crisis) — Section title says 'el siglo XX y hoy' but politics stops at 2001. No Kirchners, Macri, Milei; grieta is one Pro tip card. → Add a class '2003 to today': Néstor and Cristina Kirchner, Macri, Milei and the chainsaw, what 'kirchnerista/K', 'macrista', 'libertario' mean, how to stay out of the grieta. Present both sides as contested. _(Learners hear these names daily; 'y hoy' promises them and they are absent.)_
- **high** `missing` (new class: café) — Coffee appears only as 'order a cortado and stay two hours' (buenos-aires/iconos-de-la-ciudad). → Add 'Ordering at a café': café, cortado, lágrima, café con leche, submarino, 'con dos medialunas', the free soda water and cookie, tostado, breakfast is sweet and small, calling the mozo. _(Ordering coffee is a daily act and the words are not guessable.)_
- **high** `not_relevant` tab balance — 88 classes: food and drink 23 (mate 6, asado 6, comida 6, alfajores 5), history 13, language 13, football 7; daily-life practical (costumbres + buenos-aires) 11. → Cap niche sections at 4-5 classes and spend the freed effort on a new 'Vida diaria' section (money, SUBE, safety, café, housing, trámites). _(Depth follows what is fun to write, not what a newcomer needs.)_
- **high** `experience` section order (scripts/culture/build.mjs) — Order: mate, asado, comida, alfajores, futbol, tango, musica, habla, dichos, puteadas, costumbres, buenos-aires, regiones, iconos, historia x2. → Open with what a newcomer needs: costumbres, buenos-aires (plus new daily-life classes), habla, comida, mate, asado, futbol, puteadas, dichos, musica, tango, regiones, alfajores, iconos, historia x2. _(First 23 classes are food and drink; greetings are 11th, the city 12th, money last.)_
- **high** `experience` pensar-en-dolares — 'Money today: thinking in dollars' is class 5 of the last section (class 88 of 88). → Move it out of history into a daily-life section near the top, together with the new paying class. _(The most practical class in the tab is the hardest one to find.)_
- **medium** `missing` el-orden — Cuts taught: asado de tira, vacío, entraña, achuras. Nothing about ordering at a parrilla restaurant. → Add a class 'At the parrilla (restaurant)': bife de chorizo (not sausage), ojo de bife, lomo, parrillada para dos, papas fritas, ensalada mixta, 'jugoso / a punto / cocido', sharing portions. _(Most tourists eat asado in a restaurant first; bife de chorizo confuses everyone.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: protests and strikes) — No mention of paro, piquete, corte or marcha as part of daily life (only historic cacerolazo and 24 March). → Add 'Paro, piquete, marcha': transport strikes announced the day before, street blockades downtown, how locals check and re-plan, why protest is seen as normal civic life. _(A strike or blocked avenue will change a visitor's day in the first month.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: renting and living) — Housing only as 'flats are priced in dollars' (pensar-en-dolares) and quincho (asado/el-fuego). → Add 'Finding a place': 'dos ambientes', PH, expensas, garantía, depósito, the encargado, piso and departamento ('4° B'), timbre, rent adjusted by inflation. _(Many learners want to live there; rental words and rules are unique to Argentina.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: public health and education) — Free public university and hospitals are never mentioned; only 'oldest university' in regiones/cordoba. → Add 'Free school, free hospital': UBA and public universities without fees, guardapolvo blanco, public hospital vs obra social vs prepaga, the guardia, the farmacia de turno. _(A point of national pride and a practical need for anyone staying longer.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: gender and diversity today) — No LGBT, feminism or dating content beyond telo and chamuyo cards (habla). → Add 'Ni Una Menos and the rainbow': equal marriage 2010 (first in Latin America), gender identity law, green and light-blue pañuelos, 'chicos/chiques' debate, how flirting changed (piropo no longer welcome). _(Central to Argentina today and directly affects how a foreigner should behave.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: dating and couples) — Dating is absent; 'gordo/gorda' pet name is in costumbres/sin-filtro, telo in habla/vesre-re-posta. → Add 'Dating': 'salir', 'estamos saliendo' vs 'novios', histeriqueo, who pays, meeting the family at the Sunday asado very early, 'mi amor/gordi', WhatsApp double check etiquette. _(Social life goal of many learners; current coverage is scattered jokes.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: trámites) — Bureaucracy appears only as a punchline ('Hecha la ley, hecha la trampa', 'two-hour line at the bank'). → Add 'Trámites': sacar turno, DNI/CUIL, fotocopias, 'se cayó el sistema', the número at the counter, Migraciones, why a 'gestor' exists, patience phrases. _(Anyone staying over 90 days meets this; it is a real cultural experience.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: pampa and coast) — Classes: overview, Noroeste, Cuyo, Córdoba, Litoral, Patagonia. No pampa, Buenos Aires province, Atlantic coast, Tigre. → Add 'The pampa and la Costa': estancias and día de campo, San Antonio de Areco, Tigre and the Delta, Mar del Plata and the January exodus, carpas, churros on the beach, Punta del Este. _(Where porteños actually go on weekends and summer holidays is the one region missing.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: family and friends) — Family is scattered (Sunday pasta, abuela's flan, living with parents in a telo card). No class on it. → Add 'Family and friends': Sunday lunch at the grandparents, living at home till late 20s, friends from school for life, 'la juntada', nicknames (Negro, Gordo, Flaco, Colo), saying 'te quiero' to friends. _(Friendship and family rules explain most invitations a newcomer receives.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: drinks) — Drinks are scattered: Malbec (cuyo), fernet (cordoba), moscato (pizza), liso (litoral). → Add 'What to drink': birra (porrón, litro, pinta, sharing one bottle), vino con soda or hielo, sifón, vermut hour, fernet con coca ratio, Gancia, tap water is fine, 'agua con o sin gas'. _(Ordering a drink is basic; today the learner must finish Regiones to learn 'un tinto'.)_
- **medium** `missing` (new class: popular saints and beliefs) — Religion = Pope Francis (iconos) and Gilda's shrine (musica). No Gauchito Gil, Difunta Correa, Luján, San Cayetano. → Add 'Saints of the road': red Gauchito Gil shrines, water bottles for Difunta Correa, walking to Luján, San Cayetano queue on 7 August, cinta roja against envy, martes 13. _(Travellers see red roadside shrines everywhere and nothing explains them.)_
- **medium** `not_relevant` section — Section 'Alfajores y dulces' (5 classes) sits 4th in the tab, beside 'La mesa argentina' (6 classes). → Either merge into comida as 2 classes (alfajores+kiosco, facturas+postres) or rename the section 'Dulces y panadería' so the title matches its content. Move the kiosco content to daily life. _(Alfajores alone do not deserve a top-level section; only 2 of 5 classes are about them.)_
- **medium** `not_relevant` section — 8 classes, the longest section: first peoples, viceroyalty, May/July, San Martín, unitarios, Desierto, boats, granary. → Cut to 5: merge 'antes-de-buenos-aires' + 'virreinato-e-invasiones'; merge 'mayo-y-julio' + 'san-martin-y-belgrano'; keep Rosas/gauchos, Desierto, boats; fold granary highlights into boats. _(School-textbook history gets more space than anything a learner will live today.)_
- **medium** `not_relevant` la-tabla-y-el-descenso — Whole class on relegation, 'promedio' maths and VAR debates. → Shrink to two cards inside 'la-hinchada' ('irse a la B', Boca never went down) and drop the promedio explanation. _(Too niche for a non-fan learner; football already has 7 classes.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` buenos-aires/iconos-de-la-ciudad + comida/horarios-y-mesa — BA: 'The waiter won't bring the check until you ask. Bringing it early would feel like kicking you out.' / Comida option: 'Bringing it unasked would be like kicking you out' → Keep it in comida (it is the quiz there). In the Tortoni card say only 'order a cortado and stay two hours; nobody will rush you'. _(Same fact, same wording; the earlier card gives away the later question.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` buenos-aires/moverse + dichos/filosofia-criolla — BA: 'people line up along the wall: la cola. It's sacred.' / Dichos explain: 'The fila del colectivo is sacred.' → Keep the card in moverse; in dichos change the question to another viveza example. Use one word for the line (cola) in both. _(Same fact taught twice with two different words for it.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` dichos/filosofia-criolla + puteadas/gil-forro-chanta — Dichos: 'Pull it off and you're a vivo. In dichos keep 'viveza criolla' and say only 'the one who falls for it is the gil'. _(The gil/vivo pair is explained in full in two sections.)_

In regiones/el-interior keep size, 23 provinces, micro, fiestas; drop the porteño-vs-province pride cards. _(Two opening classes make the same point about porteños and the provinces.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` all sections — 29 cards/explains lean on 'the story goes' / 'legend says', 8 more end with 'nobody can prove it' / 'historians doubt it'. → Keep legend-questions to max one per section; prefer questions about what the learner will do or see ('what happens next?'). _(The legend-then-debunk formula becomes predictable and teaches unverified trivia.)_
- **medium** `experience` section — title: 'Historia: el siglo XX y hoy' → Either add the 2003-today class or rename to 'Historia: de Perón al 2001'. _('y hoy' promises the present, but the story stops in 2001-2002.)_
- **medium** `fact_wrong?` el-diez + messi-y-qatar — 'Three World Cups so far: 1978, 1986 and 2022.' The Messi class ends with Qatar 2022. → The 2026 World Cup has been played (June-July 2026). Check the result and update the count, and add a card on 2026 and the 2021/2024 Copa América wins. _(Content looks frozen in 2023; a football-mad learner will notice at once.)_
- **medium** `experience` escritores — Card: 'Alfonsina Storni… took her own life in the sea at Mar del Plata' followed directly by the quiz about Manuelita the turtle. → Put Alfonsina before Cortázar, or add a transition card; do not go from suicide to a children's song on the next tap. _(Breaks the spec rule: heavy topics need a transition, no tragedy-to-joke jump.)_
- **medium** `experience` vida-portena — title: 'Five things you'll notice in your first week' (class covers seven: furia, psychologists, paseaperros, Corrientes, El Ateneo, motochorro, ¡ojo!) → Rename 'Things you'll notice in your first week' or cut to five; El Ateneo is not something you 'notice', move it to iconos-de-la-ciudad. _(Title promises five; the class is a grab-bag of seven unrelated items.)_
- **medium** `experience` question format — Every one of the 88 classes is the same loop: card, guess, card, guess (185 choice questions, always 3 options, almost always 2 per class). → Vary a few per section: a true/false, an 'order the steps' (cebar, asado order), a 'what do you say?' gap in Spanish, or a 2-option dilemma. _(After 20 classes the rhythm is fully predictable; no Spanish production at all.)_
- **medium** `experience` practical vs trivia — Many classes end with a 'Pro tip' (31) but most questions test trivia (dates, origins, records) rather than behaviour. → Aim for at least one 'what do you do / say?' question per class, as in mate/la-ronda and asado/sos-invitado. _(The best classes test behaviour; the weaker ones are pub-quiz facts quickly forgotten.)_
- **low** `missing` (new class: other sports) — Non-football sport is two cards in iconos/iconos-de-hoy (Ginóbili, Vilas). → Add one class: Los Pumas, Las Leonas, polo, pato as official national sport, Fangio and Colapinto, pádel boom, Del Potro and Sabatini. _(Useful small talk; current coverage is two historical cards.)_
- **low** `missing` (new class: truco) — The card game truco is never mentioned. → Add 'Truco': Spanish deck, lying is the game, '¡Truco!' '¡Quiero!' 'Envido', secret face signs to your partner; played at asados and beaches. _(The national card game; an easy, fun guess-first class tied to asado and viveza.)_
- **low** `missing` (new class: humor, TV and streaming) — Screen culture = two Oscars and Darín. No humor or TV. → Add one class: Les Luthiers, Fontanarrosa, Capusotto, Mirtha's lunches and Susana, Tinelli, Gran Hermano, streaming channels (Olga, Luzu) everyone quotes. _(References locals drop daily; explains jokes a learner will not get.)_
- **low** `missing` (new class: today's immigrants and minorities) — Immigration ends around 1910 (los-barcos); indigenous and Afro-Argentines are one line each. → Add 'Who is Argentine today': Bolivian verdulerías, Paraguayan and Venezuelan arrivals, 'el chino' supermarket, Once and the Jewish community, Koreans in Flores, indigenous communities now. _('We came from the boats' is corrected in one line but today's mix is never shown.)_
- **low** `missing` el-calendario — Calendar covers Día del Amigo, spring, long weekends, birthdays. No Carnaval, Semana Santa, Día de la Madre (October), Día del Niño. → Add 2-3 cards or a class: Carnaval long weekend and murgas, Easter (rosca, empanadas de vigilia), Mother's Day in October, school year March-December, winter holidays in July. _(The 'very full calendar' promised in the section summary is thin.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` mas-alla-de-buenos-aires — Leprosos/canallas, pinchas/triperos nickname origins. → Keep one card ('outside BA the local clásico matters more') in de-que-cuadro-sos; drop the class or make it optional. _(Club-nickname etymology is fan trivia, not something a newcomer needs.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` mate-en-el-barrio — Class on Uruguay, Brazil's chimarrão, Paraguay's UNESCO tereré and Syria as top buyer. → Reduce to one 'Did you know?' card (Uruguay drinks more, Syria buys most) in another mate class. _(A class about other countries in a tab meant to explain Argentina.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` asados-del-pais — Vaquillona con cuero, the Viale festival, chivito, disco de arado. → Keep cordero patagónico and the disco as cards elsewhere; replace the class with 'At the parrilla restaurant'. _(Rare festival dishes a learner will almost never meet, while restaurant ordering is missing.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` inventos-y-nobeles — Vucetich's fingerprint murder case, Agote's citrate transfusion, Leloir's sugars. → Keep birome and salsa golf (things you say and eat); cut Agote and the Necochea murder, or move to one 'Did you know?' card. _(National-pride trivia with nothing the learner will see, hear or say.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` orquestas-y-piazzolla — D'Arienzo, Di Sarli, Pugliese, Troilo, Nadia Boulanger in one class. → Keep Piazzolla (Libertango, 'eso no es tango') and the red carnation; drop the bandleader list. _(Bandleader styles are for dancers, not for a general learner.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` refranes — The card itself says: 'A refrán is an old proverb, and most came from Spain.' → Replace pan-Hispanic proverbs (a caballo regalado, pájaro en mano, del dicho al hecho) with Argentine ones, or cut the class. _(Generic Spanish proverbs are not Argentine culture and exist in any textbook.)_
- **low** `not_relevant` habla + dichos + puteadas — Three language sections, 13 classes, in a tab the spec defines as 'about culture, not words'. → Merge into one 'Cómo hablamos' section of about 8 classes; push pure phrase lists (dichos/expresiones-del-dia, mas-que) to the Words hub. _(Overlaps the Words hub and crowds out life topics.)_
- **low** `repetitive` buenos-aires/vida-portena + comida/pizza-portena — BA: 'Avenida Corrientes is the city's Broadway: theaters, bookshops open late, pizza at midnight.' / Comida: 'Avenida Corrientes, the theater street, is also the pizza street.' → Keep the pizza part only in comida; in BA mention theaters and bookshops. _(Same street, same theater-and-pizza idea in two sections.)_
- **low** `repetitive` buenos-aires/vida-portena + habla/manos-y-chat — BA: 'The word you'll hear most in your first week: ¡Ojo!, literally "eye!"' / Habla: 'Finger pulling down your lower eyelid: careful, ¡ojo!' → Put word and gesture together in habla; in BA use it without re-teaching ('¡Ojo con el celu!'). _(¡Ojo! is introduced as new in both sections.)_
- **low** `repetitive` habla/lunfardo + historia-nacimiento/los-barcos + tango/nacido-en-el-arrabal — Habla: 'crammed into tenements called conventillos' / Historia: 'Many ended up in conventillos: old houses split into single rooms' / Tango: 'the arrabal… tenements' → Explain the conventillo once (los-barcos); elsewhere use the word with a three-word gloss. _(The conventillo is described from scratch three times.)_
- **low** `repetitive` comida/herencia-italiana + comida/helado + habla/sho-y-che + habla/lunfardo + historia-nacimiento/los-barcos — 'Huge waves of Italian immigrants arrived' / 'Italian immigrants brought their helado' / 'the huge wave of Italian immigrants around 1900' / 'packed with immigrants, mostly Italians and Spaniards' / 'millions of Europeans, mostly italianos' → Fine as one-line links, but vary them: only los-barcos should tell the wave story; others just say 'Italian'. _(The same immigration sentence opens five different classes.)_
- **low** `repetitive` asado/sos-invitado + costumbres/la-hora-argentina — Asado: 'Guests bring vino, drinks, dessert or hielo.' / Costumbres: 'Never show up empty-handed… Bring wine or dessert anyway.' Both also teach arriving late. → Keep the general rule in costumbres; in asado keep only the asado-specific part (ice, who buys the meat). _(Guest etiquette is taught twice.)_
- **low** `repetitive` mate/la-ronda + tango/la-milonga — Mate: 'You hand the mate back and say "gracias". What happens next?' / Tango: 'Your partner says "gracias" after the first song. What just happened?' → Keep both facts but make one a card, or link them in one line ('like in the mate round'). _(Identical trick question in two sections; the second is no longer a surprise.)_
- **low** `repetitive` buenos-aires/moverse + habla/lunfardo — BA: 'The city bus is the colectivo, but everyone calls it bondi.' / Habla question: 'The city bus is the bondi. Where does the word come from?' → Keep one: either the taxi-driver origin of the colectivo (BA) or the tram origin of the word (habla), with a pointer line in the other. _(Two origin questions about the same bus.)_
- **low** `repetitive` tango/nacido-en-el-arrabal + musica/cumbia-y-cuarteto + mate/mate-en-el-barrio — 'In 2009 UNESCO listed it as heritage' / 'UNESCO added cuarteto to its list' (answer cites tango 2009) / 'in 2020 UNESCO listed its tereré' → Keep UNESCO for tango only; give cuarteto a different surprise question. _(UNESCO-listing is used as the 'wow' fact three times.)_
- **low** `repetitive` all sections — About 20 cards end on the same joke: 'each swears theirs is best', 'a national debate', 'they'll defend it to the death', 'ask two Argentines: three opinions', 'will remind you'. → Keep the 3-4 best (leña vs carbón, Salta vs Tucumán, manteca vs grasa) and vary the rest. _(The 'Argentines argue about everything' punchline wears thin and is a stereotype.)_
- **low** `repetitive` all sections — Name-origin questions despite the spec's 'no word origins': gallinas, leprosos, triperos, arbolito, bondi, RKT, ficha, Caminito, Mafalda's M, birome, Buenos Aires, 'Desierto'. → Keep origins only where the origin is the story (Desierto, ficha); swap the rest for situation questions. _(Too many quizzes are etymology guesses with unguessable answers.)_
- **low** `experience` sin-filtro — title 'No filter', summary 'Body comments, money talk, and the gauchada' → Move the two gauchada cards to a friends/favors class; keep this class about directness (body, money, age, salary). _(A gauchada is not 'no filter'; the class ends on an unrelated topic.)_
- **low** `experience` guisos-y-helado — slug 'guisos-y-helado', title 'Stews and corn' (helado is now its own class); sits between Italian food and helado. → Rename slug to 'guisos-y-maiz' and move the class after 'empanadas' so the criollo dishes sit together. _(Stale slug and odd order: Italian, criollo stews, then Italian helado again.)_
- **low** `experience` class order — Order: cuadro, hinchada, talk, la-tabla-y-el-descenso, el-diez, messi-y-qatar, mas-alla. → Put el-diez and messi-y-qatar right after de-que-cuadro-sos; the relegation and provincial-derby classes last. _(Maradona and Messi are what every learner wants; they come 5th and 6th.)_
- **low** `experience` class titles — 'Bondi, subte, tacho' · 'Comics, cartoons and snow' · 'Diego, 1986 and the pioneers' · 'The gear' · 'The calendar' · 'Everyday expressions' · 'The writers' → Say what you get: 'Getting around: bus, subte, taxi' · 'Comics and El Eternauta' · 'Maradona and 1986' · 'Your mate kit' · 'Days Argentines celebrate' · 'Phrases you'll hear before lunch' · 'Borges, Cortázar and Manuelita'. _(Some titles need words the learner has not learned yet; others are flat.)_
- **low** `experience` section titles — Section titles in Spanish ('La mesa argentina', 'Cómo hablamos', 'Las provincias', 'Historia: el nacimiento de un país') while class titles mix English and Spanish. → Pick one rule: Spanish section title + English summary is fine, but then keep class titles in English except real phrases ('¿De qué cuadro sos?'). _(Beginners cannot read long Spanish section titles; the mix looks unplanned.)_
- **low** `experience` section summaries — alfajores: 'the snack that runs on sugar' · mate: 'The drink that runs the country' · futbol: 'Not a sport here. A religion with a fixture list.' · alfajor card: 'That's the whole religion.' · dichos: 'how Argentines really talk' → Rewrite with concrete content, e.g. alfajores: 'Dulce de leche, facturas and what to buy at the kiosco'; dichos: 'Sayings for exams, bores and bad luck'. _('Runs on' and 'religion' clichés repeat; dichos summary duplicates the habla section's promise.)_
- **low** `experience` question explains — futbol/la-tabla: 'Relegation often uses the promedio, explained next.' · puteadas: 'Forro, by far. Here's why.' · futbol: 'Welcome to the gastada.' · puteadas/boludo: 'Here's how that happened.' → Let the explain give the answer in one full sentence; the next card can add detail. _(An explain that only says 'see next card' leaves a wrong guess unexplained.)_
- **low** `experience` buenos-aires focus — Customs are stated as national ('In Argentina you…') but describe Buenos Aires: boliche hours, vos to everyone, late dinner, sh sound. → Add 'in Buenos Aires' where it matters, and one card in regiones on what differs (siesta, earlier nights, usted more common). _(A learner going to Salta or Mendoza gets porteño rules presented as national.)_
- **low** `fact_wrong?` costumbres/salir-de-noche + asado/chori-y-salsas — Costumbres: 'Getting home at six… An after keeps the party going once the boliche closes.' / Asado: 'It's 5 a.m. and the boliche just closed.' → Use the same closing time in both (around six). _(Small contradiction about when the boliche closes.)_
- **low** `weird?` salir-de-noche — 'You get to Tomi's at nine. What do you find?' → 'Tomi in pajamas, having dinner' (comida says dinner is around ten) → 'Tomi just out of the shower, nothing ready' _(Dinner in pajamas at nine clashes with 'dinner around ten' taught in comida.)_

## Talking with Pancho (AI)


### hablar-ai

- **high** `experience` SILENCE / isSilenceHallucination — "música" in SILENCE, matched with k.includes(...) on any line under 60 chars → Remove "música" from SILENCE (or match it only when it is the whole transcript). Keep substring matching only for the long phrases ("gracias por ver el video", "subtítulos realizados por"). _(A learner who says "Me gusta la música" is treated as silence and told "No te escuché".)_
- **high** `tip_wrong` FEEDBACK_SYSTEM example 6 — Line: "La cuenta es en la mesa?" → corrected "¿Me traés la cuenta a la mesa?" … why_en "*es en la mesa* means "is on the table"." → Replace with: corrected "¿La cuenta está en la mesa?", spans [{"from":"es","to":"está"}], severity "target", why_en "For where something is, use *estar*: *está en la mesa*.", better "¿Me traés la cuenta, por favor?". _(Example rewrites the whole line and guesses intent, breaking its own "fix only the errors" rule; the explanation is also wrong.)_
- **high** `tip_unclear` SYSTEM + offendingSpanish check — "Never mention or use tú forms or vosotros." + any quoted *tienes*/*aquí* rejects the explanation → fallback "The answer is *X*. You wrote *Y*." → Allow quoting the learner's own words. New rule: "If the learner used a tú/usted form or a non-Argentine word, say so: 'In Argentina it is *tenés*, not *tienes*.' Never recommend tú forms." In code, skip denylist words that appear in the learner's answer. _(The most typical mistake in this course (tú for vos, aquí for acá) can never be explained.)_
- **high** `level` PERSONA # Ending — "Bueno, me tengo que ir. ¡Fue un gusto! Nos vemos." → "Bueno, me tengo que ir. ¡Un gusto! Nos vemos." and add a role-fitting one: "¡Gracias! Chau, hasta luego." (a waiter or shopkeeper does not say "me tengo que ir"). _(The model copies examples; "Fue" is a past tense, banned at A1 "including your goodbye".)_
- **high** `experience` CHAT_SECONDS / CLOSE_SOON_SECONDS / WRAP_SECONDS — CLOSE_SOON 100 s, WRAP 150 s, hard stop 180 s for every level; wall clock includes Pancho's 0.75x audio and model wait → Close by exchanges, not seconds (close-soon at 6, wrap at 8), or give A1/A2 about 4 minutes. Do not run the clock while Pancho is thinking or speaking. _(A slow beginner gets 3–4 turns, then the daily chat (one of 3 free) is gone. Prompt promises 5–8 exchanges.)_
- **high** `experience` Correction (has_error false) + FEEDBACK_SYSTEM — Green "Correct" under any line with has_error false, e.g. "Quiero un café con milk", "¿Tú tienes la cuenta?", a garbled transcript → Add a third verdict to the schema, e.g. verdict: "correct" | "error" | "note" | "unclear". Show "Correct" only for "correct"; for English words/tú/Spain words show "Try: …" with the better line; for garbled show nothing. _(Learner is told English words, tú forms and misheard lines are "Correct".)_
- **high** `missing?` transcribe(): language_code "es" — form.append("language_code", "es") — every recording is forced to Spanish → Let the recogniser detect es/en (or retry without the forced language when confidence is low). If the line is English, pass it to Pancho marked as English so he can give the Spanish for it. _(A beginner who answers in English gets nonsense Spanish text; the "learner slips into English" rule never works.)_
- **high** `missing` LEVEL_NOTES A1 / PERSONA — A1: "Speak as you would to a friendly foreigner who has studied a few weeks. One simple question per reply." → Add: "Ask either/or or yes/no questions the learner can answer in one or two words (¿Querés café o té?). If they answer in English, with one word, or seem lost, do not repeat the same question: say it shorter, offer two answers to choose from, and accept a one-word answer warmly." _(Nothing tells Pancho how to rescue a total beginner; open questions like "¿Qué te gusta hacer?" stall them.)_
- **medium** `level` PERSONA (# How you talk) vs LEVEL_GRAMMAR A1/A2 — "Perdón, no te escuché bien, ¿me lo repetís?" · "Contame mejor…" · "politeness comes from … ¿me podrías…?" · voseo list "decime, contame, vení" → Give A1-safe examples: "Perdón, no te entiendo bien. ¿Me lo repetís?", "Uh, de eso no hablo, che. ¿Hablamos de otra cosa?", politeness: "¿me traés…?, ¿me decís…?, por favor". Say that examples above the level must be rephrased. _(Persona examples use past, commands and conditional that the A1/A2 block forbids; the model copies examples.)_
- **medium** `level` PERSONA / LEVEL_NOTES A1 — "Keep each reply short: one to three sentences, at most 40 words" (same for all levels) → Per level: A1 "one or two sentences, at most 15 words, one question"; A2 "at most 25 words"; B1/B2 "at most 40 words". _(Forty words at 0.75 speed is a long speech for a learner with a few weeks of Spanish.)_
- **medium** `missing` runTurn notes / SIMPLIFY_NOTE trigger — SIMPLIFY_NOTE only when hints were used on two turns in a row → Also send it when the last line was English, one or two words, "no entiendo/¿cómo?", or followed an empty recording; keep it on for the rest of the chat. _(Most stuck learners do not press Hint twice; they go quiet or answer in English.)_
- **medium** `missing` sessionBlock # Level — Level block has only grammar; A1 says "the most common words only" (HLD §4.6 planned "tenses taught, word list") → Add the words the learner has met: for unit chats the unit's forms; otherwise a short core list per level. Tell Pancho: "Prefer these words; any other word must be very common and guessable." _(Grammar is limited but vocabulary is not, so Pancho can still speak above a beginner's level.)_
- **medium** `missing` sessionBlock # Scenario (unit chats) — Pancho gets setting, role and key phrases; the scene's goals are written by SCENE_SYSTEM but never passed on → Add a line: "Without saying so, steer the scene so the learner gets to do these: <goals>." For unit chats also add the unit's grammar focus. _(A unit's Speaking lesson may never make the learner use what the unit taught.)_
- **medium** `experience` PERSONA # How you talk (AI question) — "if they do, say briefly that you are a practice partner and carry on" → "if they ask, say honestly and briefly that you are an AI made for practising (\"Sí, soy una inteligencia artificial para practicar español\") and carry on." _(Dodging a direct "are you an AI?" question is dishonest and confusing.)_

### hablar-scenarios

- **high** `missing` whole file / levels — Only 8 scenarios exist for A1 and A2; depto, devolucion, peluqueria, cena are B1 only; entrevista, reclamo, alquiler, sobremesa are B2 only → Add A2 versions of depto ("No hay agua caliente"), peluqueria, cena; B2 versions of depto, devolucion, cena; B1 versions of alquiler (visit + ask basics) and reclamo _(A B1 learner has no higher version of 4 scenes; beginners get only 8 scenes and finish them fast.)_
- **high** `missing` missing scenario: farmacia — No pharmacy scene ("perdido" looks for a pharmacy but never enters it) → New scenario, A1–B2: say what hurts ("Me duele la cabeza"), ask for something without prescription, ask how to take it, B1+: "¿Necesito receta?" / obra social discount _(Getting sick is the most common real need for a traveller.)_
- **high** `missing` missing scenario: taxi / Uber / llegada al aeropuerto — No taxi or ride scene → New scenario, A1–B2: give the address ("Voy a Thames y Gorriti"), ask the price, pay; B1: driver takes a long route or chats about football; airport version from Ezeiza _(It is the first conversation every visitor has in Argentina.)_
- **high** `missing` missing scenario: caja del súper / chino — No supermarket checkout scene → New scenario, A1–B1: cashier asks "¿Efectivo o tarjeta?", "¿Débito o crédito?", "¿En cuotas?", "¿Tenés la tarjeta del súper?", "¿Querés bolsa?"; learner answers and asks for QR / cash discount _(Fast cashier questions are what learners fail on every day.)_
- **medium** `fact_wrong` kiosco / A1 / goals.pay + key_phrases[3] — Pagá con transferencia / ¿Te puedo pagar con transferencia? → Goal: "Preguntá si podés pagar con tarjeta" (en: Ask if you can pay by card). Phrase: "¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?" + keep cash option "Te pago en efectivo." _(A1 is the Tourist: no Argentine bank account, cannot transfer. Tourists pay cash or card.)_
- **medium** `weird` kiosco / B1 / key_phrases[3] — ¿Te molesta si te pago en efectivo? / Do you mind if I pay cash? → "Bueno, te pago en efectivo. ¿Tenés cambio?" / "OK, I'll pay cash. Do you have change?" _(No kiosquero minds cash; cash is what they prefer. The real issue is change.)_
- **medium** `fact_wrong` colectivo / A1 / goals.sube + key_phrases[1] — Preguntá si podés pagar con la SUBE / ¿Se puede pagar con la SUBE? → Goal: "Preguntá cómo se paga el colectivo" (en: Ask how you pay on the bus). Phrase: "¿Se puede pagar en efectivo o necesito la SUBE?" _(SUBE is the normal way; nobody asks this. The real tourist question is whether cash works (it does not).)_
- **medium** `missing` colectivo / A1 + A2 — No phrase to tell the driver where you are going → Add key phrase: "Hasta La Boca, por favor." / "To La Boca, please." (what you say to the chofer when you get on) _(On a porteño bus you must tell the driver your destination before tapping the SUBE.)_
- **medium** `es_wrong` colectivo / A2 / key_phrases[2] — ¿Me avisás cuando llegamos? → "¿Me avisás dónde me bajo?" (A2-safe) or "¿Me avisás cuando lleguemos?" _(Future "cuando" needs subjunctive (lleguemos). The app records this as a model phrase.)_
- **medium** `level` verduleria / A1 / goals.best — Preguntá qué fruta está rica hoy (no key phrase covers it) → Add key phrase: "¿Qué fruta está rica hoy?" / "Which fruit is good today?" (replace "Quiero un kilo de manzanas." or "Nada más, gracias.") _(An A1 learner cannot build this question alone; it is the only goal with no model phrase.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` perdido / setting_en + role_en (all versions) — so you ask a neighbor / a neighbor from the barrio / a neighbor walking his dog → "so you ask a local" / "a man who lives in the barrio" / "a local walking his dog" _(In English "neighbor" means your own neighbor; here "vecino" is a stranger who lives in the area.)_
- **medium** `missing` cafe + parrilla — No tipping or payment habits in either restaurant scene → Add to parrilla A2/B1: "¿Puedo dejar la propina con la tarjeta?" · "¿Cobran cubierto?" · "¿Puedo pagar con QR?" · "¿Tienen descuento en efectivo?" _(Tip (10%, usually cash), cubierto charge, QR and cash discount are daily real questions.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` cafe B2 + parrilla B2 (also verduleria B1, devolucion, reclamo) — cafe B2: cold coffee, complain to waiter, get compensated · parrilla B2: overcooked steak, complain to waiter, get compensated → Change one: e.g. parrilla B2 = you are the host of a big table: choose cuts for everyone, ask about a wine, split the bill between cards _(Two B2 scenes are the same chat; 5 of 20 scenes are complaints.)_
- **medium** `repetitive` B2 versions: kiosco, colectivo, conocer B1, free B2 — "Compará con los precios de tu país" · "Compará el transporte de acá con el de tu ciudad" · "Compará algo de acá con tu país" · "¿En tu país también...?" (2 openers) → Keep one "compare with your country" goal; give the others different tasks (tell a story, give advice, plan something) _(Same task and same opener question in several scenes; feels like one conversation repeated.)_
- **medium** `experience` B1/B2 goals across file — "sin enojarte" · "con buena onda" · "sin pelearte" · "con un chiste" · "con humor" (x2) · "con elegancia" · "con tacto" · "sin quedar mal" · "sin bajonearte" → Make each goal an action you can see in the text: "Pedí que te traigan otro", "Decí por qué no querés ir", "Despedite y agradecé" _(Tone goals cannot be checked reliably in a short chat; the learner does not know when they are done. Many third goals are just "end nicely".)_
- **medium** `experience` conocer / B2 / goals — Contá una anécdota de un viaje · Defendé tu opinión con humor · Salí de la charla con elegancia → Give Pancho a topic in role_es (e.g. "opina que Buenos Aires es la mejor ciudad del mundo") and make goal 2 "Decí por qué no estás de acuerdo" _(Opinion about what? Goals have no link to the opener (bride's or groom's side).)_
- **medium** `weird` entrevista / B2 / key_phrases[0] + keyterms — En mi último laburo coordinaba un equipo de cinco personas. → "En mi último trabajo coordinaba un equipo de cinco personas." (remove "laburo" from this scene) _("Laburo" is too casual for an HR interview; it teaches the wrong register.)_
- **medium** `missing` entrevista / B2 — "Negociá el sueldo" with no real interview words → Add keyterms/phrase: "pretensión salarial", "en blanco", "sueldo bruto / neto (en mano)" — e.g. "Mi pretensión salarial es de ... en mano." _(Every Argentine interview asks "¿Cuál es tu pretensión salarial?"; the learner must know it.)_
- **medium** `missing` alquiler / B2 / key_phrases — "garantía" and "depósito" are only keyterms; no phrase about guarantee or rent increases → Add: "No tengo garantía propietaria, ¿aceptás un seguro de caución?" and "¿Cada cuánto se actualiza el alquiler?" _(For a foreigner, the guarantee and how often rent goes up are the two real problems.)_
- **medium** `fact_wrong?` devolucion / B1 / goals.choose + key_phrases[2] — Elegí entre un cambio o la devolución / Preferiría que me devuelvan la plata. → Goal: "Pedí un cambio o que te devuelvan la plata"; add to role_es: "primero ofrece cambio o nota de crédito, no plata"; add keyterm "nota de crédito" _(Argentine shops rarely give money back; they offer a swap or store credit. The learner should push for it.)_
- **medium** `missing` missing scenario: hotel / Airbnb check-in — No accommodation scene for the Tourist level → New scenario, A1–B1: check in, ask Wi-Fi password and check-out time, report "no anda el aire / no hay agua caliente" _(Core tourist situation, easy at A1.)_
- **medium** `missing` missing scenario: heladería / panadería / empanadas — No ice-cream, bakery or take-away scene → New scenario, A1–A2: "Un cuarto de helado: dulce de leche y limón", "Media docena de facturas", "Una docena de empanadas: seis de carne..."; choose flavours and amounts _(Very Argentine, simple, fun, and teaches docena / cuarto / gustos.)_
- **medium** `missing` missing scenario: médico / guardia — No doctor scene → New scenario, A2–B2: ask for a turno, describe symptoms and since when, understand instructions; B2: guardia, prepaga / obra social paperwork _(Newcomers need it and it is stressful without practice.)_
- **medium** `missing` missing scenario: me robaron / perdí algo — No emergency scene → New scenario, B1–B2: your phone was stolen: explain what happened, where and when, at the comisaría or to a friend; ask what to do _(Phone theft is a common real event in Buenos Aires; learners need the words.)_
- **medium** `missing` missing scenario: trámites (migraciones, banco, chip de celular) — No paperwork or phone-line scene for the Newcomer level → New scenarios, A2–B2: buy a SIM ("Quiero un chip prepago"), ask what documents you need for residency / DNI, open an account _(Paperwork is the main fight of anyone who moves to Argentina.)_
- **medium** `missing` missing scenario: bar / birra con amigos — No bar or drinks scene; social scenes are all "meet a stranger" or "plan the weekend" → New scenario, A1–B2: order at the bar ("Una pinta de IPA"), invite a round, split the bill ("¿Hacemos una vaquita?", "Te lo paso por Mercado Pago") _(Paying between friends by transfer is where "transferencia" really belongs.)_
- **low** `not_argentine?` kiosco / A1 / opener — ¡Hola! ¿Qué necesitás? → "¡Hola! ¿Qué te doy?" (en: "Hi! What can I get you?") _(A kiosquero says "¿Qué te doy?" or "Decime"; "¿Qué necesitás?" sounds like a help desk.)_
- **low** `level` kiosco / A2 / goals.several vs key_phrases[0] — Goal: Pedí tres cosas distintas · Phrase: Dame dos alfajores y una gaseosa, por favor. → Phrase: "Dame dos alfajores, una gaseosa y unas papas fritas." (or goal: "Pedí dos cosas distintas") _(Goal asks for three different things; the model phrase only shows two.)_
- **low** `fact_wrong?` kiosco / B2 / opener + key_phrases[0] — ¿Viste cómo aumentó todo esta semana? / la semana pasada estaba mucho más barato → "¿Viste lo que aumentó todo este año?" / "Uh, el mes pasado estaba mucho más barato." _(Weekly price jumps were 2023; today prices rise by the month. Dates the content.)_
- **low** `weird?` colectivo / A2 / opener — Te veo mirando el mapa. ¿Adónde vas? → "Te veo medio perdido. ¿Adónde vas?" / "You look a bit lost. Where are you going?" _(Nobody carries a map on a bus today; they look at the phone.)_
- **low** `level` colectivo / A1 / key_phrases[0] vs goals.which — ¿Qué colectivo me lleva a La Boca? → "¿Qué colectivo va a La Boca?" _(Simpler for A1 and matches the goal wording ("qué colectivo va a La Boca").)_

- **low** `en_wrong` verduleria / A2 / key_phrases[1] + goals.amounts (en) — a quarter of onions / a quarter of another → "a quarter kilo of onions" / "a quarter kilo of another" _("A quarter of onions" is not clear English; "un cuarto" means a quarter kilo.)_

- **low** `en_hard` verduleria / A1 / opener (en) — Morning! What'll it be today? → "Good morning! What would you like today?" _("What'll it be" is an idiom; house style is plain English.)_

## Dropped as false alarms


### input-artifact: verb forms without their own gloss (the app shows sentence meanings) (34)

- **medium** `en_wrong` como-te-llamas + quien-es / NEW WORDS llamo, llamás, llama — llamo=to be called (llamarse); llamás=to be called (llamarse); llama=to be called (llamarse) → llamo=(I) call — in 'me llamo'; llamás=(you) call — in 'te llamás'; llama=(he/she) calls — in 'se llama'. Or drop the bare forms and keep only the chunks. _(Three different conjugated forms share one infinitive gloss, so the cards teach nothing and look like duplicates.)_
- **high** `en_wrong` practico-castellano / NEW WORDS ayudás — ayudás=to help → ayudás=you help _(Gloss gives the infinitive meaning for a vos form; every other vos form says 'you ...'.)_
- **high** `en_wrong` la-hora / NEW WORDS vemos — vemos=to see (ver) → vemos=we see (ver) _('vemos' is the nosotros form, not the infinitive. The gloss teaches a wrong meaning.)_
- **medium** `level` queres-podes-vas (whole unit) — 33 new words: 16 verb forms + 13 new infinitives (hablar, tener, ser, hacer, comer, vivir, aprender, estar, escribir, ver, entender, abrir, saber) + si, conmigo, adónde, boliche, cine → Split: (1) ir + salir + places to go, (2) poder/querer + infinitive. Each infinitive gets 4 sentences now, which is thin. _(The biggest grammar step so far is packed into one unit with a one-line table tip.)_
- **medium** `tip_unclear` preferis-salir / pienso, pensás, piensa, creo, creés — Gloss 'I think, I plan to'; every pensar sentence means 'plan to'; no tip covers pensar or creer → Add a tip: 'pienso + infinitive = I plan to; creo que... = I think that...'. Add pensar to the e→ie table. Add 1-2 'think' uses: '¿Vos qué pensás?', 'Pienso mucho en vos'. _(Two new verbs with special patterns and no explanation. 'Think' meaning of pensar is never shown.)_
- **high** `en_wrong?` la-rutina, me-despierto-temprano, que-te-gusta-hacer / NEW WORDS bare forms — levanto=to get up; levantás=to get up; acuesto=to go to bed; baño=to shower, to bathe; despierto=to wake up; apuro=to hurry; juntamos=to get together → Hide these bare-verb entries from the learner, or gloss them correctly as part of the phrase (me levanto = I get up). 'Baño' alone is 'bathroom', 'despierto' alone is 'awake', 'levanto' alone is 'I lift'. _(Conjugated forms glossed as infinitives, and without 'me/te' they mean something else.)_
- **medium** `experience` la-pasamos-barbaro / NEW WORDS pasé, pasaste, pasamos — pasé=to have a (good or bad) time; pasaste=to have a (good or bad) time; pasamos=to have a (good or bad) time → Remove these three entries (la pasé / la pasaste / la pasamos already cover them), or gloss them as conjugated forms. _(Conjugated forms glossed as an infinitive, and they duplicate the 'la pasé' cards.)_
- **medium** `experience` me-duele, me-dolio / NEW WORDS duele, duelen, dolió, dolieron — duele=to hurt; duelen=to hurt; dolió=to hurt; dolieron=to hurt → duele=hurts; duelen=hurt (more than one thing); dolió=hurt (past); dolieron=hurt (past, more than one) — or drop them, since me duele / me dolió are taught. _(Four different forms all show the same infinitive gloss; learner cannot tell them apart.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` las-tareas + quien-lavo / NEW WORDS toca, tocó — toca=to touch; to play (an instrument); to be someone's turn · tocó=to touch; to play (an instrument); to be someone's turn → toca=it's (someone's) turn · tocó=it was (someone's) turn. Put the other meanings in a note on the lemma tocar. _(A conjugated form is glossed with infinitive meanings, two of them not used in the unit.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` tipo-ocho / NEW WORDS encontramos — encontramos=to meet (up) (encontrarse) → Delete this entry (duplicate of 'nos encontramos=we meet, let's meet'), or gloss it 'we meet (with nos)'. _(A conjugated form glossed as an infinitive, and it duplicates the entry before it.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` me-puse-nervioso / me-olvide / me-mude / en-lo-de-la-abuela NEW WORDS — puse=to get, to become (a feeling); enojé=to get angry; mudé=to move (house); juntábamos=to get together; sentí=to feel; olvidé=to forget → Hide these bare-form entries from the learner, or gloss the real form: 'me puse = I got', 'me mudé = I moved'. - **medium** `en_wrong` el-celu / NEW WORDS quedé, quedaste, cortó — quedé=to be left, to stay; quedaste=to be left, to stay; cortó=to cut out, to go out (power) → quedé=I was left, I stayed; quedaste=you were left, you stayed; cortó=it cut out. - **medium** `en_wrong` te-doy-la-razon / new words: equivoqué, equivocás — equivoqué=to be wrong, to make a mistake; equivocás=to be wrong, to make a mistake → Remove these two fragment entries (me equivoqué / te equivocás already cover them), or gloss them as forms: equivoqué=I was wrong (with me), equivocás=you're wrong (with te). _(A conjugated fragment is glossed as an infinitive; alone it is not a usable word.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` me-pone-nervioso-que + deberias-tomarte-unos-dias / new words: enoja, alegra, animo — enoja=to make angry; alegra=to make happy; animo=to dare, to go for it → Drop the bare fragments (me enoja / me alegra / me animo are already taught), or gloss as forms: enoja=makes angry, alegra=makes happy, animo=I dare. _(Same problem: conjugated piece shown with an infinitive meaning; confusing word card.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` se-alquila / se-aceptan-tarjetas / voy-entendiendo / me-cae-bien — NEW WORDS — vende=to sell; venden=to sell; aceptan=to accept, to allow; hacen=to do, to make; arreglan=to fix; permite=to allow; prohíbe=to ban; caen=to fall → Gloss the form, not the infinitive: vende=sells; venden=(they) sell; aceptan=(they) accept; hacen=(they) do/make; arreglan=(they) fix; permite=allows; prohíbe=bans; caen=(they) fall. Or hide these helper forms from the learner. _(Conjugated forms are glossed as infinitives; a learner tapping the word gets the wrong meaning.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` me-encargo-que, resulta-que, para-colmo, se-la-cree / NEW WORDS — portara=to behave; enteré / enteraste / enteró / enteramos / enteraron=to find out; cree=to be full of oneself; bancó=to handle it; arreglo=to manage, to get by → Remove these fragment entries (keep the full forms "me portara", "me enteré", "se la cree", "se la bancó", "me las arreglo"). _(Half-forms with infinitive glosses are wrong on their own: "cree" is not "to be full of oneself", "arreglo" is not "to manage".)_
- **high** `en_wrong` estoy-podrido + me-pudri / NEW WORDS cansé, pudrí, harté, quejo — cansé=to get tired, to get sick of · pudrí=to get fed up; to rot · harté=to get fed up · quejo=to complain → Remove these fragment entries; keep only 'me cansé', 'me pudrí', 'me harté', 'me quejo'. _(Half a reflexive verb shown as a word, with an infinitive gloss for an 'I' form.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` el-cuarto-oscuro / word: llamaron — llamaron=to call (llamar) → llamaron=they called (llamar) — or remove it from this unit's new words; it is not election vocabulary. _(Conjugated form glossed as infinitive; a basic verb form listed as new at C1.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` me-robaron, me-afanaron, se-tapo-la-pileta / word glosses — robaron=to steal, to rob · afanaron=to steal, to swipe · estafaron=to scam, to swindle · tapó=to get clogged · trabó=to get stuck, to jam · descuidé=to let your guard down → robaron=they stole · afanaron=they stole (slang) · estafaron=they scammed. Delete the stand-alone 'tapó', 'trabó', 'descuidé' cards: they only exist as 'se tapó', 'se trabó', 'me descuidé'. _(Past forms glossed as infinitives; 'tapó/trabó/descuidé' alone mean something else or nothing.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` tendria-que-haber + me-hubiera-gustado / NEW WORDS arrepiento, arrepentí, arrepentís, arrepintió — arrepiento=to regret; to change one's mind · arrepentí=to regret; to change one's mind · arrepentís=… · arrepintió=… → Remove these bare-form word cards (me arrepiento / me arrepentí / te arrepentís / se arrepintió already exist), or gloss them as 'I regret', 'I regretted', 'you regret', 'he/she regretted'. _(Conjugated forms without 'me/te/se' are not words, and an infinitive gloss on them is wrong.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` me-hizo-reir, me-mori-de-risa, no-te-lo-tomes-a-mal, se-merece-el-ascenso / NEW WORDS — reí=to laugh; reímos=to laugh; reís=to laugh; rió=to laugh; ofendiste=to offend; merece=to deserve; merecemos=to deserve → reí=I laughed; reímos=we laugh, we laughed; reís=you laugh; rió=he/she laughed; ofendiste=you offended; merece=deserves; merecemos=we deserve _(Conjugated forms are glossed as infinitives; learner tapping the word gets the wrong person and tense.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` se-instalaron-en-la-boca + caiste / NEW WORDS — escaparon=to get out, to escape; instalaron=to settle; instaló=to settle; picó=to get touchy → Remove these half-entries (keep only 'se escaparon', 'se instalaron', 'se instaló', 'se picó'), or gloss them as past forms: 'they escaped', 'they settled', 'he/she settled'. _(Past-tense forms glossed as infinitives; duplicate of the reflexive entry.)_
- **medium** `en_wrong` NEW WORDS in se-caso, se-recibio, me-emocione, se-emociono, gracias-por-todo — casó=to get married; recibió=to graduate; jubiló=to retire; murió=to die; emocioné=to be moved; adapté=to adapt; despido=to say goodbye → Hide these pronoun-less entries from the learner, or gloss them truthfully (despido = 'I fire / dismissal', recibió = 'he received'). _(A conjugated form without its pronoun is glossed as an infinitive; alone it means something else.)_

### app shuffles quiz options (4)

- **high** `experience?` all classes / every choice except two — `correct: 0` on 11 of 12 questions in mate.yaml and 10 of 12 in asado.yaml → Check that the app shuffles options at render time; if not, vary the correct index in the YAML. _(If options show in file order, the first answer is almost always right and guessing is pointless.)_
- **medium** `experience?` all classes / every choice page — correct: 0 on all 11 questions (same in comida.yaml, 14 questions) → Confirm the app shuffles options at display time; if not, vary the correct index in the yaml. _(If options are not shuffled, the first option is always right and guessing is pointless.)_
- **medium** `experience?` all classes (also regiones.yaml) — Every choice page in both files has `correct: 0` → Confirm the app shuffles options at display time; if not, vary the correct index in the YAML. _(If options are shown in file order the first answer is always right, which kills the guessing game.)_
- **low** `experience?` all classes — correct: 0 on every one of the 18 questions (both files) → Confirm the app shuffles options. If not, vary the correct index. _(If not shuffled, the first option is always right.)_
